(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-113-6, as read from the print "೧-೧೧೩-೬".) *(Read letter by letter; the Kannada reading of the second line is doubtful: "ajīr" / "ajīgar" given as "ajīgaḥ" [?] — taken exactly as printed.)* — in these ṛks too Uṣas is the one addressed. Here also, in the present ṛk, this word is used to show that she, and she alone, is the helper of the moving about of beings: "you for strength (*kṣatrāya*), you for fame (*śravase*), you ... for going (*ityai*)".

***urviyā*** — *uruśabdāt tṛtīyaikavacane urviyā iti rūpam | uruṇā iti | uruśabdāt tṛtīyā vibhaktyekavacane prayuktāyāṃ urviyā*: from the word *uru*, in the instrumental singular, the form is *urviyā*; its meaning is "widely": the sense "extending everywhere, spreading and pervading".

> व्यचस्वतीरुर्विया वि श्रयन्तां पतिभ्यो न जनयः शुम्भमानाः ।
> देवीर्द्वारो बृहतीर्विश्वमिन्वा देवेभ्यो भवत सुप्रायणाः ॥

> *vyacasvatīrurviyā vi śrayantāṃ patibhyo na janayaḥ śumbhamānāḥ |*
> *devīrdvāro bṛhatīrviśvaminvā devebhyo bhavata suprāyaṇāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-5 [?], as I read the print; the OCR shape agrees.) — as it is used in this ṛk and similar ones, so here also: "may Uṣas, pervading widely, spread out and shine".

> इन्द्रं कक्षीवदेवं [?] च प्रौषसे पृथुरुत्तरे ।

> *indraṃ kakṣīvadevaṃ [?] ca prauṣase pṛthuruttare |*

(Bṛ. De. 3-140 [?], as read; the first words of the pāda are doubtful in the print.) — that the two Sūktas Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-123 and 1-124 are addressed to the deity Uṣas is the statement of the *Bṛhaddevatā*.

> तथाश्विनशस्त्रे इदमादिसूक्तद्वयस्य विनियोगः ।

> *tathāśvinaśastre idamādisūktadvayasya viniyogaḥ |*

(Sā. Bhā. Pīṭhikā, Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-123.) — thus Sāyaṇa has stated the *viniyoga* of this Sūkta and of the preceding (1-123) Sūkta. In this context, since the connection that exists between the Āśvina-śastra and the present ṛk must be understood, the nature of the Āśvina-śastra and its narrative context is described. Then Prajāpati laid down a condition that the thousand mantras known as the Āśvina-śastra be recited, and that it should not fall short of that. As a cart-wheel, once it is smeared with oil, turns smoothly, so after drinking ghee (*kṛtapāna*) the mantras can be recited smoothly; therefore one must first drink ghee and afterwards recite. And just as a bird, ready to fly, makes its body light, so the suitor of her must have that quality [of lightness].

> तस्मिन्देवा न समजानत ममेदं ममेदमस्त्विति ते संजानाना अब्रुवन्नाजिमस्यायामहे स यो न उज्जेष्यति तस्येदं भविष्यतीति तेऽग्नेरेवाधि गृहपतेरादित्यं काष्ठामकुर्वत तस्मादाग्नेयी प्रतिपद्भवत्याश्विनस्याग्निर्होता गृहपतिः स राजेति ।

Then the gods, not agreeing among themselves (each saying "let her be mine, let her be mine"), all came together for one agreement: "In the race, whoever wins — to him she belongs"; and they went to a single race-ground. Then, starting from Agni, the *gṛhapati*, they ran as far as the Sun. Therefore the first mantra is the one addressed to Agni:

> स त्वं दक्षस्यावृको वृधो भूर्यः परस्यान्तरस्य तरुषः ।

Then the two Aśvins approached Agni and asked: "Give us the way; help us to win in this race." Agni agreed, and asked that he too be given a share in the victory; therefore in the Āśvina-śastra there is a portion for him too. Afterwards the two Aśvins followed Uṣas: "Give us the way; help us to win in this race." Then the goddess Uṣas agreed, and laid down the condition that she too have a share in their victory; they consented, and the Āśvina-śastra therefore contains the recitation of the Sūkta addressed to Uṣas. In the same way the Aśvins asked Indra as well, and made him a sharer in this.

The connection that exists between the present Sūktas 1-123 and 1-124 and the Āśvina-śastra is as stated above.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, Ṛk 1; noted briefly, sūtra numbers as read by the OCR).** *ucchantī* — root *uchī vivāse*, Tudādi class; śatṛ in the laṭ sense; when the feminine is intended, *ugitaś ca* (Pā. 4-1-6) gives ṅīp, and the augment *num*; the accent of the verb-suffix remains. *udyan* — prefix *ut*, root *iṇ gatau*; śatṛ; *śap* with *luk*; *iṇo yaṇ* (Pā. 6-4-81) gives *yaṇ* to the root; the suffix is acute on its first syllable; in the compound the accent of the final member's own nature. *sūryaḥ* — root *ṣū preraṇe*; *suvati karmaṇi lokaṃ preryati iti sūryaḥ*; *rājasūyasūrya…* (Pā. 3-1-114) records it as formed with *kyap* and the augment *ruṭ*. *urviyā* — the word *uru*; with the instrumental singular following, the vārttika *iyāḍiyāj…upasaṃkhyānam* (Pā. 7-1-39 vārttika [?]) gives *iyāc*, and *yaṇ*; *citaḥ* (Pā. 6-1-163) gives the final-acute by the accent of the suffix. *aśret* — root *śriñ sevāyām*; *chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ* gives laṅ in the present sense, the third person singular *tip*, with loss of the *i*; *bahulaṃ chandasi* gives *luk* of *śap*; *sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ* gives guṇa of the root-vowel; since it follows a non-verb word, the *nighāta* accent. *savitā* — root *ṣū preraṇe*; *tṛc* in the agent sense; *ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ* gives the augment *iṭ*; guṇa of the root-vowel and *av*; since *tṛc* has the marker *c* it is final-acute; nominative singular. *asāvīt* — root *ṣū prasavaiśvaryayoḥ*; *chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ* (Pā. 3-4-6 as read by the OCR) gives luṅ in the sense of loṭ, the second person singular [as printed "ಪ್ರಥಮಪುರುಷ" — third person singular] *tip*; elision of the *i*; *siC* for the *ṅ* [sic, as I read it]; *āstisico 'prkte* (Pā. 7-3-96, the print "೬-೩-೮೬"? — numerals doubtful [?]) gives the augment *īṭ*; *sicivṛddiḥ parasmaipadeṣu* (Pā. 7-2-1) gives vṛddhi; then *āvādeśa*; *iṭo 'ṭi* (Pā. 8-2-28) elides the *siC*; the augment *aṭ* to the stem; since it follows a non-verb word, the *nighāta* accent. *dvipat* — *dvau pādau asya dvipāt*; *saṃkhyāsupūrvasya* (Pā. 5-4-140) elides the end of the word *pāda*; as a samāsānta; *ayasmayādīni* [as printed "ಆಯಸ್ಮಯಾದೀನಿ" (Pā. 1-4-20)] gives *bha*-designation; so *pādaḥ pat* (Pā. 6-4-130) …

#### Ṛk 2

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अमिनती दैव्यानि व्रतानि प्रमिनती मनुष्या युगानि ।
> ईयुषीणामुपमा शश्वतीनामायतीनां प्रथमोषा व्यद्यौत् ॥ २ ॥

> *aminatī daivyāni vratāni praminatī manuṣyā yugāni |*
> *īyuṣīṇāmupamā śaśvatīnāmāyatīnāṃ prathamoṣā vyadyaut ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अमिनती । दैव्यानि । व्रतानि । प्रऽमिनती । मनुष्या । युगानि ।
> ईयुषीणाम् । उपऽमा । शश्वतीनाम् । आऽयतीनाम् । प्रथमा । उषाः । वि । अद्यौत् ॥ २ ॥

> *aminatī | daivyāni | vratāni | pra 'minatī | manuṣyā | yugāni |*
> *īyuṣīṇām | upa 'mā | śaśvatīnām | ā 'yatīnām | prathamā | uṣāḥ | vi | adyaut ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> दैव्यानि व्रतानि देवसंबन्धीन्यग्निहोत्रादीनि कर्माणि । व्रतमिति कर्मनाम । व्रतं कर्वरमिति तन्नामसु पाठात् । तानि कर्माण्यमिनती अहिंसन्ती भानप्रदानेनानुकूलं कुर्वती । तथा मनुष्या मनुष्याणां युगानि युगोपलक्षितान्निमेषादिकालावयवान्प्रमिनती प्रकर्षेण हिंसन्ती । आयुः क्षपयन्तीत्यर्थः । यद्वा । युगानि युगानि परस्परसंयोगं प्रमिनती हिंसन्ती । वियोगं कुर्वतीत्यर्थः ।

> *daivyāni vratāni devasaṃbandhīnyagnihotrādīni karmāṇi | vratamiti karmanāma | vrataṃ karvaramiti tannāmasu pāṭhāt | tāni karmāṇyaminatī ahiṃsantī bhānapradānenānukūlaṃ kurvatī | tathā manuṣyā manuṣyāṇāṃ yugāni yugopalakṣitānnimeṣādikālāvayavānpraminatī prakarṣeṇa hiṃsantī | āyuḥ kṣapayantītyarthaḥ | yadvā | yugāni yugāni parasparasaṃyogaṃ praminatī hiṃsantī | viyogaṃ kurvatītyarthaḥ |*

*(Read from the image; checked against the OCR.)* "*Daivyāni vratāni* — the rites that belong to the gods, the Agnihotra and the rest. *Vrata* is a name for 'rite' (*karman*), since *vrataṃ karvaram* is read among the names of rites. Those rites *aminatī* — not harming, doing what is favourable by the giving of light. And *manuṣyā* — of men — *yugāni* — the divisions of time, beginning with the twinkling of an eye, marked by the *yuga* — *prāminatī*: she wears down exceedingly; that is, she exhausts life. Or else: *yugāni yugāni* — the pairs: *prāminatī* — she harms their mutual union; that is, she causes separation."

> उषःकाले सर्वे यथायथं स्वस्वव्यापाराय गच्छन्तीति प्रसिद्धम् । किंच ईयुषीणां गच्छन्तीनामतीतानां शश्वतीनां नित्यानामुषसामुपमा । ताभिः सदृशीत्यर्थः । सादृश्यं च सदृशीरद्य सदृशीरिदु श्व इत्युक्तम् । ऋ. १-१२३-८ । तथायतीनां प्रथमागामिनीनामुषसां प्रथमभाविनी सती व्यद्यौत् । विशेषेण प्रकाशते । यद्वा । ईयुषीणां गमनशीलानां पश्वादीनां शश्वतीनां संततिप्रवाहरूपेण नित्यानामुपमा । तत्सन्निभेत्यर्थः । तथायतीनां रात्र्यवसानसमय उत्पद्यमानानां प्रज्ञावागादीनां प्रथमा प्रथमभाविनी । उषस्यागतायां वाचो बुद्धयश्च स्फुरन्तीति प्रसिद्धम् । तादृशी देवी व्यद्यौत् । प्राणिनामनुग्रहाय द्योतते ॥

> *uṣaḥkāle sarve yathāyathaṃ svasvavyāpārāya gacchantīti prasiddham | kiṃca īyuṣīṇāṃ gacchantīnāmatītānāṃ śaśvatīnāṃ nityānāmuṣasāmupamā | tābhiḥ sadṛśītyarthaḥ | sādṛśyaṃ ca sadṛśīradya sadṛśīridu śva ityuktam | ṛ. 1-123-8 | tathāyatīnāṃ prathamāgāminīnāmuṣasāṃ prathamabhāvinī satī vyadyaut | viśeṣeṇa prakāśate | yadvā | īyuṣīṇāṃ gamanaśīlānāṃ paśvādīnāṃ śaśvatīnāṃ saṃtatipravāharūpeṇa nityānāmupamā | tatsannibhetyarthaḥ | tathāyatīnāṃ rātryavasānasamaya utpadyamānānāṃ prajñāvāgādīnāṃ prathamā prathamabhāvinī | uṣasyāgatāyāṃ vāco buddhayaśca sphurantīti prasiddham | tādṛśī devī vyadyaut | prāṇināmanugrahāya dyotate ‖*

*(Read from the image; the reference "ऋ. १-१२३-८" is as printed and agrees with the OCR; "sadṛśīr adya sadṛśīr idu śvaḥ" is read as printed.)* "At the time of Uṣas it is well known that all go, each as is fitting, to his own business. Moreover she is the *upamā* — the likeness — of the past Uṣases, *īyuṣīṇām* — those that have gone — *śaśvatīnām* — the everlasting: that is, she is like them. The likeness has been stated in 'such dawns today, such dawns tomorrow' (Ṛ. 1-123-8). Likewise, being first (*prathamā*) among the Uṣases that are to come (*āyatīnām*, the first-coming), she shines (*vi adyaut*) — she shines specially. Or else: she is like *īyuṣīṇām* — the beasts and the like that move about — *śaśvatīnām* — everlasting by their continuous flow of progeny; that is, she resembles them. And *āyatīnām* — of the knowledge, speech and the rest that arise at the end of the night — she is the first, the first to appear; for it is well known that when Uṣas has come, speech and intellect stir to life. Such a goddess has shone; she shines for the favour of living beings."

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *Daivyāni* — belonging to the gods; *vratāni* — the rites, Agnihotra and the like; *aminatī* — not harming (since she is a giver of light, favourable); *manuṣyā* — of men; *yugāni* — the divisions of time beginning with the twinkling of the eye, or the pairs (couples); *prāminatī* — [she] who wears down exceedingly (causes decay), or who separates each from each; *īyuṣīṇām* — of those that have gone, or that are of a moving nature (and); *śaśvatīnām* — to the everlasting (Uṣases), or to living beings (everlasting by the continuity of progeny); *upamā* — like; *(tathā — and likewise)* *āyatīnām* — of the Uṣases that are to come, or of (wisdom and speech) that arise at the time of Uṣas; *prathamā* — the first, or the one standing at the beginning; *uṣāḥ* — goddess Uṣas; *vi adyaut* — shone well (shone for the favour of beings).

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** The goddess Uṣas does not obstruct the rites of the gods, the Agnihotra and the rest; but she wears away the lives of men. She, like those Uṣases who went before and who are everlasting (like those that are continuous in the flow of progeny), shone well as the first of the Uṣases to come (the first at the time of dawn for the wisdom and speech of waking beings, for their favour).

**Printed English (as printed):** *Unimpeding divine rites, although wearing away the ages of mankind, the Dawn shines the similitude of the (mornings) that have passed, or that are to be for ever, the first of those that are to come.*

An English critic named Bloomfield describes the poetic idea and the style of composition of this ṛk as follows [printed in English]:

> *There can be no question that I. 124.2. is the source of the repeated padas in I. 92. 11 and 12. The antithesis between* अमिनती *and* प्रमिनती *and* ईयुषीणां *and* आयतीनां *cannot but be intentional and primary. Note also the parallelism between* अमिनती *and* आयतीनां; *and* प्रमिनती *and* ईयुषीणां. *On the other hand, we ought to allow full weight to the really senseless non-sequitur of the second distich in I. 92. 11. reducing the ages of men, the woman shines by the light of her paramour (the sun). 'For the meaning of Yuga 'age' i. e. 'period of time' see Bal Gangadhar Tilak. The Arctic Home in the Vedas.*

> **There can be no question that I. 124.2. is the source of the repeated padas in I. 92. 11 and 12. The antithesis between* aminatī *and* praminatī *and* īyuṣīṇāṃ *and* āyatīnāṃ *cannot but be intentional and primary. Note also the parallelism between* aminatī *and* āyatīnāṃ; *and* praminatī *and* īyuṣīṇāṃ. *On the other hand, we ought to allow full weight to the really senseless non-sequitur of the second distich in I. 92. 11. reducing the ages of men, the woman shines by the light of her paramour (the sun). 'For the meaning of Yuga 'age ' i. e. 'period of time ' see Bal Gangadhar Tilak. The Arctic Home in the Vedas.**

> *Stanza I. 124.2 is the high-water mark of Vedic composition. The two antitheses* अमिनती…………प्रमिनती *and* ईयुषीणां…………आयतीनां *mark as later imitations all repetitions that disturb this balance. The relation of the two pairs of antithetical words may be expressed in the proportion:* अमिनतीः आयतीनां :: प्रमिनती ईयुषीणां. *That is to say: the dawns preserve the laws of the Gods (*अमिनती*) by their regular appearance (*आयतीनां*); the ages of men waste away (*प्रमिनती*) as the dawns fade day by day.*

> **Stanza I. 124.2 is the high-water mark of Vedic composition. The two antitheses* aminatī…………praminatī *and* īyuṣīṇāṃ…………āyatīnāṃ *mark as later imitations all repetitions that disturb this balance. The relation of the two pairs of antithetical words may be expressed in the proportion:* aminatīḥ āyatīnāṃ :: praminatī īyuṣīṇāṃ. *That is to say: the dawns preserve the laws of the Gods (*aminatī*) by their regular appearance (*āyatīnāṃ*); the ages of men waste away (*praminatī*) as the dawns fade day by day.**

(Rig-Veda Repetitions, Vol. I, p. 108.) *(Reproduced as printed; the Devanagari words inside the quotation are printed in the Kannada script in the source, in the hand of the printer, and are given here in Devanagari. The printed punctuation, "pădas", "Yuga ' age'" and the stray quotation mark, are kept.)* Thus, in the Kannada, the idea of the two ṛks 1-92-11 and 1-92-12 is combined in this single ṛk, and the construction of the antithesis in the excellent poetic style and the expression of feeling are greatly praised.

***daivyāni vratāni aminatī*** — *daivasaṃbandhīni agnihotrādikarmāṇi ahiṃsantī | bhānapradānena anukūlaṃ kurvatī*: by giving light and by furnishing what is favourable to the sacrificer, she does not obstruct, "does not harm", the rites of sacrifice belonging to the gods — this is the sense.

***yugāni prāminatī*** — Sāyaṇa states two kinds of meaning here. The first: *yugopalakṣitān nimeṣādikālāvayavān prakarṣeṇa hiṃsantī*. The word *yuga* indicates the span of men's lives. Uṣas, by the divisions called moment, day, month and the like, wears down all the period of human life — this is the sense. Wherever the span of human life is mentioned, the use of the word *yuga* is common — as in

The first word, "marutsu"/"marutsvo", is doubtful, as is "dhṛṣṇuyā" in the print.) — and in other ṛks of this kind it may be seen. In this context the Maruts protect the sacrificer at all times; here also, and likewise in other places, the expression *mānuṣā yugā* ("the ages of men") is used.

***īyuṣīṇām upamā; āyatīnāṃ prathamā*** — *atītānāṃ nityānām uṣasāṃ (tābhiḥ) sadṛśī; āgāminīnām uṣasāṃ prathamabhāvinī*: the meaning is that she has one and the same form for all the appearances of the Uṣases — those who have gone before and those who will come ever-lasting.

In this ṛk a kind of sadness is mixed with the joy. By describing the beauty and loveliness of Uṣas, who gives consciousness and light to the whole world and fills living beings with life, the delight is expressed; and along with that, before this Uṣas, who continues ever in the state of youth, a certain agitation of mind shows itself, in the thought that humans and all other beings grow old in a short time and die. In this idea the experience of truth and the vision of beauty are joined. The vision of the truth that Uṣas wears away all the life of men is generally expressed whenever Uṣas is described. For example —

> ईयुष्टे ये पूर्वतरामपश्यन्व्युच्छन्तीमुषसं मर्त्यासः ।
> अस्माभिरू नु प्रतिचक्ष्याभूदो ते यन्ति ये अपरीषु पश्यान् ॥

> *īyuṣṭe ye pūrvatarāmapaśyanvyucchantīmuṣasaṃ martyāsaḥ |*
> *asmābhirū nu praticakṣyābhūdo te yanti ye aparīṣu paśyān ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-113-11, as printed "೧-೧೧೩-೧೧".) — in many such places those who earlier saw this everlasting beauty of Uṣas and were delighted are all gone; and the same is the fate of those who come after; but Uṣas alone is ever young and eternal: with this thought the picture of man's brief life is reflected.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 2, pp. 139–140; noted briefly, numbers as read by the OCR).** *aminatī* — root *mīñ hiṃsāyām* (Kryādi); śatṛ in the laṭ sense; *kryādibhyaḥ śnā* (Pā. 3-1-81) gives *śnā*; *svādīnām hrasvaḥ* [as printed; the OCR "Pā. 7-3-80"] shortens the root; since the suffix has the marker *p* [sic: *ś*], *śnābhyastayor ātaḥ* (Pā. 6-4-112) elides the *ā* of *śnā*; in the feminine ṅīp because it is *ugit*; the negative *naña*-tatpuruṣa compound; *tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyā…* [OCR "Pā. 6-2-2"] gives the natural accent of the first member (an indeclinable).

### Printed p. 140  (PDF 161)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 18 Sū. 124".)*

*daivyāni* — *devasya imāni daivyāni*; in the sense of relationship, *devād yajñau* [print: "ದೇವಾದ್ಯಜ್ಞೌ", Pā. 4-1-85, as read by the OCR] gives the suffix *yañ*; *yasyeti ca* (Pā. 6-4-148) elides the *a*; since the suffix has the marker *ñ*, *ñnityādir nityam* (Pā. 6-1-197) gives the first-syllable acute; accusative plural. *prāminatī* — with the prefix *pra*; the process as before. *śatur anumo nadyajādī* (Pā. 6-1-173) gives the acute accent to the *ṅīp*… [as printed: *śatur anumaḥ*]; in the compound the accent of the final member. *manuṣyā* — *manor jātāv ñyat tuk ca* (Pā. 4-1-161) [as read] gives the suffix *yat*; with it the augment *tuk*; *tit svaritam* (Pā. 6-1-185) gives the suffix the *svarita*; when the genitive plural [sic, nominative plural] follows, *supāṃ sulug* (Pā. 7-1-39) gives *ā* for it.

*īyuṣīṇām* — root *iṇ gatau*; when *liṭ* has come, *kvasuś ca* (Pā. 3-2-107) gives *kvasu*; taking it as cause the root is doubled; when the feminine is intended, *ugitaś ca* (Pā. 4-1-6) gives ṅīp; since it has the *bha* designation, *vasoḥ saṃprasāraṇam* (Pā. 6-4-131) gives *saṃprasāraṇa* with *pūrvarūpa*; since the suffix beginning with a vowel follows, *iṇo yaṇ* (Pā. 6-4-81) gives *yaṇ* to the *i* of the root; *dīrgha iṇaḥ kiti* (Pā. 7-4-69) lengthens the reduplicative syllable; *śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca* (Pā. 8-3-60) gives *ṣatva* to the *s* of *vasu*; genitive plural. As the *ṅīp* and *sup* are unaccented the accent of *vasu* remains.

*śaśvatīnām* — *ugitaś ca* (Pā. 4-1-6) gives ṅīp in the feminine; genitive plural. *āyatīnām* — prefix *ā*; root *iṇ gatau*; śatṛ in the laṭ sense; *iṇo yaṇ* (Pā. 6-4-81) gives *yaṇ*; ṅīp in the feminine; *jyāc chandasi bahulam* [as printed "ಜ್ಯಾತ್ಸಂದಸಿ ಬಹುಲಮ್" (Pā. 6-1-178)] gives the acute accent to the case-ending *nām* in the genitive plural.

*adyaut* — root *dyut dīptau*; luṅ, third person singular *tip*, with loss of the *i*; *dyudbhyo luṅi* (Pā. 1-3-91) gives *parasmaipada*; by *vyatyaya* the *luk* of *siC*; where guṇa would be expected, vṛddhi occurs in the Veda; or else from the root *dyu abhigamane*; in luṅ, *ucyato vṛddhir luki hali* [print: "ಉತೋ ವೃದ್ಧಿರ್ಲುಕಿ ಹಲಿ" (Pā. 7-3-89)] gives vṛddhi; since it follows a non-verb word, the *nighāta* accent. ‖ 2 ‖

#### Ṛk 3

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> एषा दिवो दुहिता प्रत्यदर्शि ज्योतिर्वसाना समना पुरस्तात् ।
> ऋतस्य पन्थामन्वेति साधु प्रजानतीव न दिशो मिनाति ॥ ३ ॥

> *eṣā divo duhitā pratyadarśi jyotirvasānā samanā purastāt |*
> *ṛtasya panthāmanveti sādhu prajānatīva na diśo mināti ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> एषा । दिवः । दुहिता । प्रति । अदर्शि । ज्योतिः । वसाना । समना । पुरस्तात् ।
> ऋतस्य । पन्थाम् । अनु । एति । साधु । प्रजानतीऽइव । न । दिशः । मिनाति ॥ ३ ॥

> *eṣā | divaḥ | duhitā | prati | adarśi | jyotiḥ | vasānā | samanā | purastāt |*
> *ṛtasya | panthām | anu | eti | sādhu | prajānatī 'iva | na | diśaḥ | mināti ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> एषोषा दिवो द्योतमानात्मकस्य द्युलोकस्य दुहिता दुहितृस्थानीया । तत उत्पद्यमानत्वाद्दुहितेत्युपचर्यते । पुरस्तात्पूर्वस्यां दिशि प्रति प्रत्येकमदर्शि । दृश्यते । सर्वेषामपि प्राणिनामाभिमुख्येन प्रकाशत इत्यर्थः । कीदृशी सा । ज्योतिर्वसाना तेजोरूपं वस्त्रमाच्छादयन्ती तेजसा प्रकाशयन्ती समना सम्यगानयित्री चेष्टयित्री । अन्तर्भावितण्यर्थोऽयम् । यद्वा । सह युगपदेव मन्यतेऽवबुध्यते प्राणिभिरिति समना । व्युत्पत्त्यन्तरावधारणादनवग्रहः । सा तादृशी ऋतस्यादित्यस्य पन्थां पन्थानं मेरोः प्रान्तप्रदेशमनुक्रमेण साधु सम्यगेति । गच्छति । सूर्यो यत्र यत्र गच्छति तत्र तत्र पुरस्तादुषा अपि गच्छतीत्यर्थः । सैव विशेष्यते । प्रजानतीव प्रियभूतस्य सूर्यस्य मार्गो मयापि गन्तव्य इति चेतयन्तीव । यथा लोके प्रियस्यानुरागायुक्ता काचिद्भर्तारं सर्वास्ववस्थासु न विमुञ्चति तथेयमपीत्यर्थः । किंच दिशः प्राच्यादिका न मिनाति । न हिनस्ति । किंतूषा यत्र गच्छति सा प्राचीत्येवं प्राच्यादिव्यवहारं करोतीत्यर्थः ॥

> *eṣoṣā divo dyotamānātmakasya dyulokasya duhitā duhitṛsthānīyā | tata utpadyamānatvādduhitetyupacaryate | purastātpūrvasyāṃ diśi prati pratyekamadarśi | dṛśyate | sarveṣāmapi prāṇināmābhimukhyena prakāśata ityarthaḥ | kīdṛśī sā | jyotirvasānā tejorūpaṃ vastramācchādayantī tejasā prakāśayantī samanā samyagānayitrī ceṣṭayitrī | antarbhāvitaṇyartho 'yam | yadvā | saha yugapadeva manyate 'vabudhyate prāṇibhiriti samanā | vyutpattyantarāvadhāraṇādanavagrahaḥ | sā tādṛśī ṛtasyādityasya panthāṃ panthānaṃ meroḥ prāntapradeśamanukrameṇa sādhu samyageti | gacchati | sūryo yatra yatra gacchati tatra tatra purastāduṣā api gacchatītyarthaḥ | saiva viśeṣyate | prajānatīva priyabhūtasya sūryasya mārgo mayāpi gantavya iti cetayantīva | yathā loke priyasyānurāgāyuktā kācidbhartāraṃ sarvāsvavasthāsu na vimuñcati tatheyamapītyarthaḥ | kiṃca diśaḥ prācyādikā na mināti | na hinasti | kiṃtūṣā yatra gacchati sā prācītyevaṃ prācyādivyavahāraṃ karotītyarthaḥ ‖*

*(Read from the image; checked against the OCR, whose Devanagari is garbled in the second half. A few small words — "meroḥ prāntapradeśam", "anavagrahaḥ" — are given as I read them.)* "This Uṣas is the *duhitā* — in the position of a daughter — of *divaḥ* — the shining heaven; since she arises from it she is figuratively called 'daughter'. *Purastāt* — in the eastern quarter — she is *pratyadarśi*, 'seen each one by one'; that is, she shines before the face of all living beings. What is she like? *Jyotir vasānā* — clothing herself in a garment of radiance, making things shine with brightness; *samanā* — she who well leads, who makes [beings] active (the verb *ana* here has the causative sense included); or else *samanā* — she whom living beings know, apprehend together, simultaneously; this is a derivation for which no break (*avagraha*) is given. Such a one follows well (*sādhu*) the path (*panthām*) of *ṛta*, i.e. of the Āditya — the border regions of Meru — in order; wherever the Sun goes, there Uṣas also goes in front: that is the sense. She is further described: *prajānatīva* — as if reflecting 'the path of the beloved Sun must be gone along by me too'. As in the world a woman full of love does not leave her husband in any condition, so this one: that is the sense. And *na dišo mināti* — she does not injure the quarters, east and the others; but where Uṣas goes, that is 'east' — thus she gives rise to the usage 'east' and so on."

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *Eṣā* — this; *divaḥ* — of the world of the atmosphere (heaven); *duhitā* — in the position of a daughter, the goddess Uṣas; *jyotirvasānā* — wearing a garment of light; *samanā* — [she who] makes beings well engaged in their various occupations (or [she who] shows herself to all beings at one time); *purastāt* — in the eastern quarter; *prati adarśi* — is seen one by one; (*sā* — she); *ṛtasya* — of the Āditya; *panthām* — the path (the way); *prajānatī iva* — like a woman who has understood that she must follow in all circumstances the way of her beloved; *sādhu* — well; *eti* — goes (follows); (*kiṃca* — and); *diśaḥ* — the quarters, east and others; *na mināti* — does not harm (does not destroy).

### Printed p. 142  (PDF 163)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 18 Sū. 124".)*

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** The goddess Uṣas, in the form of the daughter of heaven, wearing a garment of light, showing herself at one time (to all beings), rises in the eastern quarter; as a woman who knows that she must follow the path of her beloved, she follows well the path of Āditya; (when she thus follows) she does not obstruct the (affairs of living beings) of the quarters.

**Printed English (as printed):** *She, the daughter of heaven, is beheld in the east, gracious and arrayed in light : she travels steadily along the path of the sun, as if cognizant (of his pleasure), and damages not the quarters (of the horizon).*

**Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 3.**

In this ṛk it is described how Uṣas, the daughter of heaven, follows the path of *ṛta* and moves in a fixed course. One must consider what the "path of *ṛta*" is. Here the word *ṛta* is explained as "Āditya". Therefore scholars hold that "the path of *ṛta*" may be the zodiac (*rāśicakra*). [The following English is printed as such:]

> *"When, in the Rig-veda, the fixed Path of Rita unerringly followed by the Devas (originally the shining ones or the luminaries) is spoken of in the Rig-veda it should, in my opinion, naturally mean Zodiac or the imaginary belt or Zone in the heavens, within which the apparent motions of the Sun, moon and the Principal Planet or Devas are confined."*

(A. B. O. R. I.) *(as printed, with the source abbreviation.)* That there is some truth in this explanation is helped by the description in the ṛk which is cited below.

### Printed p. 143  (PDF 164)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 7.)*

> द्वादशारं नहि तज्जराय वर्वर्ति चक्रं परि द्यामृतस्य ।
> आ पुत्रा अग्ने मिथुनासो अत्र सप्त शतानि विंशतिश्च तस्थुः ॥

> *dvādaśāraṃ nahi tajjarāya varvarti cakraṃ pari dyāmṛtasya |*
> *ā putrā agne mithunāso atra sapta śatāni viṃśatiśca tasthuḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-11, as printed "೧-೧೬೪-೧೧".) The wheel of *ṛta* has twelve spokes; that wheel revolves around the sky; and on this wheel's path seven hundred and twenty sons stand in pairs — this is the purport of this ṛk. Probably in this description the twelve months and the three hundred and sixty days and nights are indicated.

> वेद मासो धृतव्रतो द्वादश प्रजावतः । वेदा य उपजायते ॥

> *veda māso dhṛtavrato dvādaśa prajāvataḥ | vedā ya upajāyate ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-25-8, as read from the print "೧-೨೫-೮".) — as is said in this ṛk, it may also be said that the 360 days and nights are the offspring of these twelve months.

The ṛks cited below, which describe the goddess Uṣas and her path of movement, make us acquainted with the path of *ṛta*.

> ता आ चरन्ति समना पुरस्तात्समानतः समना पप्रथानाः ।
> ऋतस्य देवीः सदसो बुधाना गवां न सर्गा उषसो जरन्ते ॥

> *tā ā caranti samanā purastātsamānataḥ samanā paprathānāḥ |*
> *ṛtasya devīḥ sadaso budhānā gavāṃ na sargā uṣaso jarante ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-51-9, as read from the print "೪-೫೧-೯".) From a certain regulated place of this *ṛta*, the goddess Uṣas, like other luminous bodies, begins her movement visible to us. If she follows this path of *ṛta* without leaving it even a little, then her straight path does not fail.

> जानत्यह्नः प्रथमस्य नाम शुक्रा कृष्णादजनिष्ट श्वितीची ।
> ऋतस्य योषा न मिनाति धामाहरहर्निष्कृतमाचरन्ती ॥

> *jānatyahnaḥ prathamasya nāma śukrā kṛṣṇādajaniṣṭa śvitīcī |*
> *ṛtasya yoṣā na mināti dhāmāharaharniṣkṛtamācarantī ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-123-9.)

> एषा स्या वेनी [?] भवति द्विबर्हा आविष्कृण्वाना तन्वं पुरस्तात् ।
> ऋतस्य पन्थामन्वेति साधु प्रजानतीव न दिशो मिनाति ॥

> *eṣā syā venī [?] bhavati dvibarhā āviṣkṛṇvānā tanvaṃ purastāt |*
> *ṛtasya panthāmanveti sādhu prajānatīva na diśo mināti ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-80-4 [?], as read from the print; the word "*vainī*"/"*venī*" is doubtful in my reading.) — the daughter of heaven, wearing a garment in the form of splendour, follows the path of *ṛta* in a straight line: thus it is described in many contexts. But what is this path of *ṛta*?

> अग्निं विश ईळते मानुषीर्या अग्निं मनुषो नहुषो वि जाताः ।
> अग्निर्गान्धर्वीं पथ्यामृतस्याग्नेर्गव्यूतिर्घृत आ निषत्ता ॥

> *agniṃ viśa īḷate mānuṣīryā agniṃ manuṣo nahuṣo vi jātāḥ |*
> *agnirgāndharvīṃ pathyāmṛtasyāgnergavyūtirghṛta ā niṣattā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-80-6, as read from the print.)

### Printed p. 144  (PDF 165)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 18 Sū. 124".)*

Since the path of this *ṛta* is the path on which the Gandharvas move, it must be in a very high place in the atmosphere. This is the path of the Āditya, and —

> उदु त्यच्चक्षुर्महि मित्रयोरा एति प्रियं वरुणयोरदब्धम् ।
> ऋतस्य शुचि दर्शतमनीकं रुक्मो न दिव उदिता व्यद्यौत् ॥

> *udu tyaccakṣurmahi mitrayorā eti priyaṃ varuṇayoradabdham |*
> *ṛtasya śuci darśatamanīkaṃ rukmo na diva uditā vyadyaut ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-51-1, as printed.)

> इदमु त्यन्महि महामनीकं यदुस्रिया सचत पूर्व्यं गौः ।
> ऋतस्य पदे अधि दीद्यानं गुहा रघुष्यद्रघुयद्विवेद ॥

> *idamu tyanmahi mahāmanīkaṃ yadusriyā sacata pūrvyaṃ gauḥ |*
> *ṛtasya pade adhi dīdyānaṃ guhā raghuṣyadraghuyadviveda ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-5-5 [?], as read; the print's middle numeral is doubtful.) *(Read letter by letter; the last two pāda words are doubtful.)* — in these ṛks the rising of the Āditya, who is of the nature of *ṛta*, and his charming form are described —

> कविर्नृचक्षा अभि षीमचष्ट ऋतस्य योना विघृते मदन्ती ।
> नाना चक्राते सदनं यथा वेः समानेन क्रतुना संविदाने ॥

> *kavirnṛcakṣā abhi ṣīmacaṣṭa ṛtasya yonā vighṛte madantī |*
> *nānā cakrāte sadanaṃ yathā veḥ samānena kratunā saṃvidāne ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-54-6 [?], as read from the print.) — in this ṛk it is described that the Sun, rejoicing in the womb (*yoni*) of *ṛta*, is watching heaven and earth. In the same way, in many other ṛks the summit and the root of *ṛta* are described —

> ऋतस्य बुध्न उषसामिषण्यन्वृषा मही रोदसी आ विवेश ।
> मही मित्रस्य वरुणस्य माया चन्द्रेव भानुं वि दधे पुरुत्रा ॥

> *ṛtasya budhna uṣasāmiṣaṇyanvṛṣā mahī rodasī ā viveśa |*
> *mahī mitrasya varuṇasya māyā candreva bhānuṃ vi dadhe purutrā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-61-7 [?], as read from the print.) — here the root-region of *ṛta*, the light of heaven and earth in that region, and the entrance of the Āditya between them, are stated. In many such contexts the Western scholars have not explained the word *ṛta* in a physical sense but everywhere only in a moral sense. But in the present ṛk (1-124-3) all this description is included, and a path of a physical orb of light which Uṣas follows is indicated.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 3, pp. 144–145; noted briefly, sūtra numbers as read by the OCR).** *divaḥ* — genitive singular; *ūḍidaṃpadādyappumrainyuvidbhyaḥ* (Pā. 6-1-171) gives the acute accent to the case-ending. *adarśi* — root *dṛśir prekṣaṇe*; in the Veda, in the present sense, in the passive, luṅ; third person singular, the ending *ta*; *ciṇ bhāvakarmaṇoḥ* (Pā. 3-1-66) gives *ciṇ* for *ci*; *ciṇo luk* (Pā. 6-4-104) elides the *ta*; with *ciṇ* as cause there is guṇa of the *ṛ* of the root; the augment *aṭ* to the stem; since it follows a non-verb word, the *nighāta* accent.

### Printed p. 145  (PDF 166)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 7.)*

*vasānā* — root *vasa ācchādane*; *śānac* in the laṭ sense; by *vyatyaya* the *luk* of *śap* does not occur; since the *sārvadhātuka* follows the *upadeśa*, *tāsyanudāttet* (Pā. 6-1-186) makes it unaccented and the root-accent remains. *samanā* — prefix *sam*, root *ana prāṇane*; as it shows a causative sense the root is of included-causative sense; *ac* in the agent sense; *ṭāp* in the feminine; *citaḥ* (Pā. 6-1-163) gives the final-acute. Or else from the root *man avabodhane*: *saha yugapad eva manyate avabudhyate prāṇibhir iti samanā*; since this derivation was not considered, no *avagraha* is shown in the pada text. *purastāt* — the word *pūrva*; *pūrvādharāvarāṇāṃ purdhavaś caiṣām* (Pā. 5-3-39) gives the suffix *astāti* and the substitution *pur* for the base; the suffix is acute on its first syllable. *panthām* — the word *pathin*; with the accusative singular following, *vyatyayo bahulam* and *pathimathyṛbhukṣām āt* (Pā. 7-1-85) give *ā*; *tho nthaḥ* changes *th* to *nth*; because the word *pathin* is formed with a suffix [Uṇ. 4-?, as printed "೪-೪೫೨" — doubtful [?]] it would be final-acute, but *pathimathoḥ sarvanāmasthāne* (Pā. 6-1-199) gives it the first-syllable acute. *eti* — root *iṇ gatau*; Adādi; laṭ third person singular; since it follows a non-verb word the *nighāta* accent. *prajānatī* — root *jñā avabodhane*; śatṛ in the laṭ sense; *kryādibhyaḥ śnā* (Pā. 3-1-81); *jñājanor jā* (Pā. 7-3-79) gives the substitute *jā*; *śnābhyastayor ātaḥ* (Pā. 6-4-112) elides the *ā* of the verb-suffix; *ugitaś ca* gives ṅīp in the feminine; *śatur anumo nadyajādī* (Pā. 6-1-173) gives the acute on the ṅīp, since it follows a śatṛ without *num*; in the compound the accent of the final member. *mināti* — root *mīñ hiṃsāyām* (Kryādi); laṭ third person singular *tip*; *śnā*; *svādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ* (as printed; the OCR "Pā. 7-3-80") shortens the root; since it follows a non-verb word, the *nighāta* accent. ‖ 3 ‖

*(This is the ṛk that was cited by number on p. 115 above, there given as "1-124-4 [?]": the number is thereby confirmed.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> एषोषाः । उपो इति निपातद्वयसमुदायात्मक एको निपातः । सर्वैः समीप एवादर्शि । दृश्यते । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । शुन्ध्युवो न वक्षः । अत्र नकार उपमार्थीय उपरिष्टादुपयुज्यमानत्वात् । यत्र तु प्रतिषेधो विवक्षितस्तत्र पुरस्तान्नकारः प्रयुज्यते । तथा च यास्कः । पुरस्तादुपाचारस्य यत्प्रतिषेधतीति । तस्योदाहरणं नेन्द्रं देवममंसतेति । उपरिष्टादपाचारस्य येनोपमिमीते इति । तस्योदाहरणं दुर्मदासो न सुरायामिति । नि. १-४ । ऋ. १०-८६-१ । ऋ. ८-२-१२ । शुन्ध्युरादित्यः सर्वेषां शोधकत्वात् । तस्य च वक्षःस्थानीयो रश्मिसमूहः । स यथा प्रकाशमानो दृश्यते तद्वदित्यर्थः । यद्वा शुन्ध्युरिति जलचरः श्वेतवर्णः पक्षिविशेषः । स यथा स्वकीयं वक्षः प्रकाशयन्दृश्यते तद्वदित्यर्थः । किंच नोधा इव प्रियाण्याविरकृत । नवनं स्तोत्रं धारयतीति नोधाः । एतन्नामा महर्षिर्देवताः स्तुतिव्याजेन नानाविधैर्मन्त्रैः प्रियाणि स्वमनीषितान्याविष्कृतवान् । तद्वदेषापि स्वकीयानि सर्वलोकस्य प्रियाणि तेजांस्याविरकरोत् । किंचाद्मसन्न । अत्राप्युपमार्थीयो नकारः । अद्यते इत्यद्मानम् । तस्य पाकाय गृहे सीदतीत्यद्मसत् । पाचिका योषित् ससतो बोधयन्ती । सा यथा स्वपतः पुत्रादीन्भोजनाय …

> *eṣoṣāḥ | upo iti nipātadvayasamudāyātmaka eko nipātaḥ | sarvaiḥ samīpa evādarśi | dṛśyate | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | śundhyuvo na vakṣaḥ | atra nakāra upamārthīya upariṣṭādupayujyamānatvāt | yatra tu pratiṣedho vivakṣitastatra purastānnakāraḥ prayujyate | tathā ca yāskaḥ | purastādupācārasya yatpratiṣedhatīti | tasyodāharaṇaṃ nendraṃ devamamaṃsateti | upariṣṭādapācārasya yenopamimīte iti | tasyodāharaṇaṃ durmadāso na surāyāmiti | ni. 1-4 | ṛ. 10-86-1 | ṛ. 8-2-12 | śundhyurādityaḥ sarveṣāṃ śodhakatvāt | tasya ca vakṣaḥsthānīyo raśmisamūhaḥ | sa yathā prakāśamāno dṛśyate tadvadityarthaḥ | yadvā śundhyuriti jalacaraḥ śvetavarṇaḥ pakṣiviśeṣaḥ | sa yathā svakīyaṃ vakṣaḥ prakāśayandṛśyate tadvadityarthaḥ | kiṃca nodhā iva priyāṇyāvirakṛta | navanaṃ stotraṃ dhārayatīti nodhāḥ | etannāmā maharṣirdevatāḥ stutivyājena nānāvidhairmantraiḥ priyāṇi svamanīṣitānyāviṣkṛtavān | tadvadeṣāpi svakīyāni sarvalokasya priyāṇi tejāṃsyāvirakarot | kiṃcādmasanna | atrāpyupamārthīyo nakāraḥ | adyate ityadmānam | tasya pākāya gṛhe sīdatītyadmasat | pācikā yoṣit sasato bodhayantī | sā yathā svapataḥ putrādīnbhojanāya …*

*(Read from the image; checked against the OCR. The Ṛg references after Ni. 1-4 — "10-86-1" and "8-2-12" — follow the OCR where the print is small; "10-86-1" is doubtful [?]. The passage continues on p. 147.)* "*Upo* — one particle made up of the two particles *upa* and *u*: she is seen quite near, by all. A comparison there: *śundhyuvo na vakṣaḥ*. Here the *na* has the sense of comparison, since it is used after [the word compared]. Where a negation is intended, the *na* is used before: and so Yāska says: '*purastād upacārasya yat pratiṣedhati*' ('when it negates what is said before'), the example of which is *nendraṃ devam amaṃsata*; and '*upariṣṭād apacārasya yenopamimīte*' ('when it is used after, for what it compares'), the example of which is *durmadāso na surāyām*" (Ni. 1-4; Ṛ. 10-86-1 [?]; Ṛ. 8-2-12). "*Śundhyu* is Āditya, since he purifies all; his bosom is the mass of rays. As it appears shining, so she: that is the sense. Or else *śundhyu* is a water-bird, a kind of white bird; as it is seen displaying its own breast, so she. Moreover, *nodhā iva priyāṇy āvir akṛta* — *navanaṃ stotraṃ dhārayatīti nodhāḥ*: the great seer of this name, with various mantras in the guise of praise of the deities, made manifest his own desired, dear things; just so this Uṣas made manifest her own radiances, dear to the whole world. And *admasan na* — here too the *na* is of the sense of comparison. *Admānam* is 'what is eaten'; she who sits in the house for its cooking is *admasat*; the woman who cooks, awakening those who sleep; as she, for the meals of her sleeping husband, sons and others, …"

### Printed p. 147  (PDF 168)

> …भोजनाय बोधयति तद्वत् । यद्वा । अद्मेति गृहनाम वरूथमद्मेति तन्नामसु पाठात् । तत्र सीदतीत्यद्मसज्जननी । सा यथा स्वपतः पुत्रादीनुषःकाले प्रबोधयति तथा भुवनाख्ये गृहे सीदन्ति तत्रत्यान्प्राणिनः प्रबोधयतीयमुषाः । ईयुषीणामागमनशीलानां स्त्रीणां मध्ये शश्वत्तमा पुनःपुनरागच्छति । प्रातर्नियतमागच्छन्तीनां वारयोषितां मध्ये स्वयमेका सती नियतमागच्छतीत्यभिप्रायः । अत्र निरुक्तम् । उपादर्शि शुन्ध्युवः शुन्ध्युरादित्यो भवति शोधनात्तस्यैव वक्षो भासोऽध्यूढमिदमपीतरद्वक्ष एतस्मादेवाध्यूढं कायै [?] । शकुनिरपि शुन्ध्युरुच्यते शोधनादेवोदकचरो भवति । आपोऽपि शुन्ध्यव उच्यन्ते शोधनादेव । नोधा ऋषिर्भवति नवनं दधाति । स यथा स्तुत्या कामानाविष्कुरुत एवमुषा रूपाण्याविष्कुरुते । अद्मसदद्मानं भवत्यसादिनीति वान्नसानिनीति वा । ससतो बोधयन्ती शश्वत्तमागात्पुनरेयुषीणां स्वपतो बोधयन्ती शाश्वतिकतमागात्पुनरागामिनीनाम् । नि. ४-१६ । इति ॥

> *…bhojanāya bodhayati tadvat | yadvā | admeti gṛhanāma varūthamadmeti tannāmasu pāṭhāt | tatra sīdatītyadmasajjananī | sā yathā svapataḥ putrādīnuṣaḥkāle prabodhayati tathā bhuvanākhye gṛhe sīdanti tatratyānprāṇinaḥ prabodhayatīyamuṣāḥ | īyuṣīṇāmāgamanaśīlānāṃ strīṇāṃ madhye śaśvattamā punaḥpunarāgacchati | prātarniyatamāgacchantīnāṃ vārayoṣitāṃ madhye svayamekā satī niyatamāgacchatītyabhiprāyaḥ | atra niruktam | upādarśi śundhyuvaḥ śundhyurādityo bhavati śodhanāttasyaiva vakṣo bhāso 'dhyūḍhamidamapītaradvakṣa etasmādevādhyūḍhaṃ kāyai [?] | śakunirapi śundhyurucyate śodhanādevodakacaro bhavati | āpo 'pi śundhyava ucyante śodhanādeva | nodhā ṛṣirbhavati navanaṃ dadhāti | sa yathā stutyā kāmānāviṣkuruta evamuṣā rūpāṇyāviṣkurute | admasadadmānaṃ bhavatyasādinīti vānnasāninīti vā | sasato bodhayantī śaśvattamāgātpunareyuṣīṇāṃ svapato bodhayantī śāśvatikatamāgātpunarāgāminīnām | ni. 4-16 | iti ‖*

*(Read from the image and checked against the OCR; the words "kāyai [?]" and "adhyūḍham" in the Nirukta passage are doubtful in the print.)* "…[so she] awakens for meals: likewise [the Uṣas]. Or else *admā* is a name for 'house' (it is read among the names *varūtham*, *admā*); one who sits there is *admasat*, the housewife. As she wakes her sleeping husband, sons and others at the time of dawn, so this Uṣas wakes the beings who dwell in the house called the world. Among the women, *īyuṣīṇām* — who go [early] — she, *śaśvattamā*, comes again and again; among the courtesans who regularly come in the morning, she alone is regular: that is the intention. Here the Nirukta: '*upādarśi śundhyuvaḥ*: *śundhyu* is Āditya, because of purifying; his bosom is *bhāsā* — what is raised by light … Also the bird *śakuni* is called *śundhyu*, because it purifies, it being a water-dweller; also the waters are called *śundhyavaḥ* because of purifying. *Nodhā* is a seer; he holds newness. As he, by praise, makes manifest his desires, so does Uṣas make forms manifest. *Admasat* — one who sits at food: *admānaṃ bhavati*, '*asādinī*', or *annasāninī*. *Sasato bodhayantī śaśvattamā āgāt punar eyuṣīṇām* — waking the sleeping, the most continual, she has come again of those who are to come back.' (Ni. 4-16)."

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *Eṣā* — this goddess Uṣas; *śundhyuvaḥ* — of the purifying Sun (or of the water-dwelling white bird); *vakṣaḥ na* — like the rays which are in the position of a bosom (as when one shows the bosom); *upo* — near; *adarśi* — is seen (by all); *nodhāḥ iva* — as the seer called Nodhas (in the guise of praise manifested all the things dear to him); *priyāṇi* — the dear special forms (of radiant form); *āviḥ akṛta* — made manifest; *admasat* — the woman who cooks food and the like; *sasataḥ bodhayantī na* — like [her] waking the sleeping children for food (waking the sleeping beings, the goddess Uṣas); *ā īyuṣīṇām* — among the women who rise and come at dawn; *śaśvattamā* — the most unfailing (regularly); *punaḥ ā agāt* — comes again and again.

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** The goddess Uṣas is seen, like the rays of the Sun, quite nearby (by all); like the seer Nodhas she takes on many forms dear to people; like a mother who, having cooked food and the like in the house, wakes her children, she wakes the sleeping beings; she rises again and again more regularly than all the women who rise early (by habit).

**Printed English (as printed):** *She is beheld nigh at hand, (radiant) as the breast of the illuminator (the sun); and, like Nodhas, has made manifest many pleasing*

### Printed p. 148  (PDF 169)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 18 Sū. 124".)*

*(objects) : like a matron she awakens (her) sleeping (children), and of all (females who are) stirring betimes, she, the most unvarying, repeatedly appears.*

**Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 4.**

For this ṛk the author of the Nirukta has made the following explanation (as above):

> उपादर्शि शुन्ध्युवः शुन्ध्युरादित्यो भवति शोधनात्तस्यैव वक्षो भासाध्यूढमिदमपीतरद्वक्ष एतस्मादेवाध्यूढं कायै [?] । शकुनिरपि शुन्ध्युरुच्यते शोधनादेवोदकचरो भवत्यापोऽपि शुन्ध्यव उच्यन्ते शोधनादेव । नोधा ऋषिर्भवति नवनं दधाति स यथा स्तुत्या कामानाविष्कुरुत एवमुषा रूपाण्याविष्कुरुते सदनं भवत्यसादिनीति वान्नसानिनीति वा । ससतो बोधयन्ती शश्वत्तमागात्पुनरेयुषीणां । स्वपतो बोधयन्ती शाश्वतिकतमागात्पुनरागामिनीनाम् ।

> *upādarśi śundhyuvaḥ śundhyurādityo bhavati śodhanāttasyaiva vakṣo bhāsādhyūḍhamidamapītaradvakṣa etasmādevādhyūḍhaṃ kāyai [?] | śakunirapi śundhyurucyate śodhanādevodakacaro bhavatyāpo 'pi śundhyava ucyante śodhanādeva | nodhā ṛṣirbhavati navanaṃ dadhāti sa yathā stutyā kāmānāviṣkuruta evamuṣā rūpāṇyāviṣkurute sadanaṃ bhavatyasādinīti vānnasāninīti vā | sasato bodhayantī śaśvattamāgātpunareyuṣīṇāṃ | svapato bodhayantī śāśvatikatamāgātpunarāgāminīnām |*

(Ni. 4-16, as printed "೪-೧೬".) *(Read letter by letter from the image; the pieces marked [?] are not clear in the print.)* And, explaining thus, he states the meanings of the word *śundhyu*: *śundhyur ādityo bhavati śodhanāt* — "the Āditya has this name because of purifying" — the first meaning; *śakunir api śundhyur ucyate śodhanād evodakacaro bhavati* — the bird that moves in water is also called by this name because it purifies by removing the dirt there; *āpo 'pi śundhyava ucyante śodhanād eva* — the water too is called by this name because it purifies: thus the various meanings of the word are shown; in all contexts the root is of one and the same sense. In the Ṛk Saṃhitā —

> प्र शुन्ध्युवं वरुणाय प्रेष्ठां मतिं वसिष्ठ मीळ्हुषे भरस्व ।
> य ईमर्वाञ्चं करते यजत्रं सहस्रामघं वृषणं बृहन्तम् ॥

> *pra śundhyuvaṃ varuṇāya preṣṭhāṃ matiṃ vasiṣṭha mīḷhuṣe bharasva |*
> *ya īmarvāñcaṃ karate yajatraṃ sahasrāmaghaṃ vṛṣaṇaṃ bṛhantam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-88-1 [?], as I read the print.) — in this ṛk *śundhyu* is an epithet of the praise, "that which purifies, or that which is pure of itself", "to be made pure, or to be pure by itself".

> युवं रथेन विमदाय शुन्ध्युवं न्यूहथुः पुरुमित्रस्य योषणाम् ।
> युवं ह वं वध्रिमत्या अगच्छतं युवं सुषुतिं चक्रथुः पुरंधये ॥

> *yuvaṃ rathena vimadāya śundhyuvaṃ nyūhathuḥ purumitrasya yoṣaṇām |*
> *yuvaṃ ha vaṃ vadhrimatyā agacchataṃ yuvaṃ suṣutiṃ cakrathuḥ puraṃdhaye ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-117-20, as read from the print.) — in this ṛk *śundhyu* means "a pure woman". In the present ṛk the appearance of Uṣas is described; it is compared to the bosom-like mass of rays of the purifier, the Sun, or to the breast of the white water-bird.

### Printed p. 149  (PDF 170)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 7.)*

***nodhā iva*** — for this word the author of the Nirukta says: *nodhā ṛṣir bhavati | navanaṃ dadhāti | sa yathā stutyā kāmān āviṣkurute.* As the seer called Nodhas makes visible, by his new praises that take the form of poetry, the wishes lying in his heart, so Uṣas too manifests her sleeping brilliance — thus it is compared.

Nodhas (Gautama) is well known as the seer of the seven sūktas in the first maṇḍala of the Ṛk-saṃhitā from the 58th to the 64th [numerals as read; the OCR gives "12 to 64"], and of the 88th sūkta of the eighth maṇḍala and the 93rd of the ninth. His story is told in many places in the Ṛk-saṃhitā itself —

> तं त्वा वयं पतिमग्ने रयीणां प्र शंसामो मतिभिर्गोतमासः ।
> आशुं न वाजंभरं मर्जयन्तः प्रातर्मक्षू धियावसुर्जगम्यात् ॥

> *taṃ tvā vayaṃ patimagne rayīṇāṃ pra śaṃsāmo matibhirgotamāsaḥ |*
> *āśuṃ na vājaṃbharaṃ marjayantaḥ prātarmakṣū dhiyāvasurjagamyāt ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-60-5, as read from the print.)

— in such ṛks, [they are] said to be "sons of Gotama" praising Agni, the lord of wealth.

> एना ते हार्योजना सुवृक्ती इन्द्र ब्रह्माणि गोतमासो अक्रन् ।
> ऐषु विश्वपेशसं धियं धाः प्रातर्मक्षू धियावसुर्जगम्यात् ॥

> *enā te hāryojanā suvṛktī indra brahmāṇi gotamāso akran |*
> *aiṣu viśvapeśasaṃ dhiyaṃ dhāḥ prātarmakṣū dhiyāvasurjagamyāt ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-61-16 [?], as read from the print.) — here it is said that the Gautama sons composed praises addressed to Indra. In the present ṛk it is described that the appearance of Uṣas was shining like the wishes revealed by praises composed by Nodhas Gautama.

***admasat*** — *admasad admānaṃ bhavaty asādinīti vā annasāninīti vā* (Ni. 4-16, as printed): The word *admā* has the name "food"; it is *admasat* either because she sits before the food in order to eat it, or because she possesses food: thus the author of the Nirukta states the explanation of this word. Sāyaṇa:

> अद्मसन्न । अत्राप्युपमार्थीयो नकारः । अद्यत इत्यद्मान्नम् । तस्य पाकाय गृहे सीदतीत्यद्मसत् । पाचिका योषित् । यद्वा अद्मेति गृहनाम । वरूथमद्मेति तन्नामसु पाठात् । तत्र सीदतीत्यद्मसज्जननी ॥

> *admasanna | atrāpyupamārthīyo nakāraḥ | adyata ityadmānnam | tasya pākāya gṛhe sīdatītyadmasat | pācikā yoṣit | yadvā admeti gṛhanāma | varūthamadmeti tannāmasu pāṭhāt | tatra sīdatītyadmasajjananī ‖*

*(Read from the image.)* "*Admasan na* — here too the *na* has the sense of comparison. What is eaten is *admā*, 'food'; she who sits in the house for its cooking is *admasat*, the woman who cooks. Or else *admā* is a name for 'house' — since *varūtham*, *admā* are read among its names; one who sits there is *admasat*, the housewife (*jananī*)." — Because food is to be eaten, *admā* means food; *admasat* means a woman who stays in the house in order to cook it; or, since the word *admā* is recorded among the names of the house, she who stays in the house, the mother (*jananī*): he states the meaning of this word in two ways. As the *na* is of the sense of comparison,

> सा जननी यथा स्वपतः पुत्रादीनुषःकाले प्रबोधयति तथा भुवनाख्ये गृहे सीदन्ति तत्रत्यान्प्राणिनः प्रबोधयतीयमुषाः ।

> *sā jananī yathā svapataḥ putrādīnuṣaḥkāle prabodhayati tathā bhuvanākhye gṛhe sīdanti tatratyānprāṇinaḥ prabodhayatīyamuṣāḥ |*

— as the mother wakes her children at the time of dawn, so Uṣas, the mother of the world, wakes all the beings in the world: that is the sense.

Or else, some scholars hold that *admasat* may also mean "the *hotṛ* priest"; and it is well known that the *hotṛ* also wakes the gods and others —

> प्र बोधयोषो अश्विना प्र देवि सूनृते महि ।
> प्र यज्ञहोतरानुषक्प्र मदाय श्रवो बृहत् ॥

> *pra bodhayoṣo aśvinā pra devi sūnṛte mahi |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-9-? [?], as read — the print's last numeral is not clear to me.) — in this ṛk Uṣas is entreated to wake the Aśvins, as the *hotṛ* of the sacrifice wakes the Aśvin deities.

> दश राजानः समिता अयज्यवः सुदासमिन्द्रावरुणा न युयुधुः ।
> सत्या नृणामद्मसदामुपस्तुतिर्देवा एषामभवन्देवहूतिषु ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-83-7, as read from the print.) — in this ṛk Sāyaṇa himself gives this meaning: *admasadām — admānnaṃ havis tatra sīdantīty admasada ṛtvijaḥ* — "the priests who sit near the oblation" — he explains, saying "priests". Likewise —

> वद्मा हि सूनो अस्यद्मसद्वा चक्रे अग्निर्जनुषाज्मान्नम् ।
> स त्वं न ऊर्जसन ऊर्जं धा राजेव जेरवृके क्षेष्यन्तः ॥

> *vadmā hi sūno asyadmasadvā cakre agnirjanuṣājmānnam |*
> *sa tvaṃ na ūrjasana ūrjaṃ dhā rājeva jeravṛke kṣeṣyantaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-4-4 [?], as read.) — in this too, and likewise in the ṛks 8-44-29 [?] and 8-43-19 [?] and others, it may be said that the word means *hotṛ*.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar, Ṛk 4; noted briefly, numbers as read by the OCR).** *śundhyuvaḥ* — root *śundha śuddhau*; *yaji-mani-śundhi-dasi-janibhyo yuc* [print: "ಯಜಿಮನಿಶುಂಧಿದಸಿಜನಿಭ್ಯೋ ಯುಚ್"] (Uṇ. 3-300 as read) gives the suffix *yu*; with the genitive singular following, *tanvādīnāṃ chandasi bahulam upasaṃkhyānam* (Pā. 6-4-77, vārttika) gives *uvaṅ*; the accent of the suffix. *nodhāḥ* — *navanaṃ dadhāti iti nodhāḥ*; "*nodhā ṛṣir bhavati navanaṃ dadhāti*" (Ni. 4-16) says Yāska; root *ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*; with *navana* as the upapada, the suffix *asun*, and *no* for the upapada; the accent of the final member. *akṛta* — root *ḍukṛñ karaṇe*; luṅ, third person singular, the ending *ta*; *mantre ghasa-hvara-…* (Pā. 2-4-80, as read) gives *luk* to the *cli*; since the suffix has the marker *ṅit*, no guṇa; the augment *aṭ*; since it follows a non-verb word, the *nighāta* accent.

*admasat* — *adyate iti admā, annam; tadarthaṃ sīdatīti admasat*; *sadiṣu* [sic; *sadiṣvañjaḥ*?] (Pā. 3-2-61 as read) gives *kvip* to the root *ṣad* when a subanta stands as upapada; *ṣatva*… of the initial of the root; *gatikārakopapadāt kṛt* (Pā. 6-2-139) gives the accent of the final member. *sasataḥ* — root *ṣasa svapne*; Adādi; śatṛ in the laṭ sense; *ṣatva* of the initial; accusative plural; since the case-ending follows a śatṛ without *num*, *śatur anumo nadyajādī* (Pā. 6-1-173) gives it the acute accent. *bodhayantī* — root *budha avagamane*; in the causative sense, *hetumati ca* (Pā. 3-1-26) gives *ṇic*; with it as cause the guṇa of the root's short penultimate vowel; after *ṇijanta*, śatṛ in the laṭ sense; *śap*; guṇa of *ṇic* and the *ay* substitute; in the feminine *num* by *ugit*; the *ṇic*-accent remains. *śaśvattamā* — suffix *tamap* in the sense of excess; since *upottamaṃ śaśvattamau sarvatra* (Pā. 6-1-160 as read) is read in the *ūḍādi* group, *tamap* though *pit* is final-acute. *agāt* — root *iṇ gatau*; Adādi; luṅ, third person singular *tip*; *itaś ca* elides the *i*; *e g(ā) luṅi* (Pā. 2-4-45) gives *gā*; *gātisthāghupābhūbhyaḥ sicaḥ parasmaipadeṣu* (Pā. 2-4-77) elides the *siC*; the augment *aṭ*; since it follows a non-verb word, the *nighāta* accent. ‖ 4 ‖

#### Ṛk 5

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> व्यू प्रथते वितरं वरीय ओभा पृणन्ती पित्रोरुपस्था ॥ ५ ॥

> *pūrve ardhe rajaso aptyasya gavāṃ janitryakṛta pra ketum |*

> वि । ऊँ इति । प्रथते । वितरम् । वरीयः । आ । उभा । पृणन्ती । पित्रोः । उपस्था ॥ ५ ॥

> *pūrve | ardhe | rajasaḥ | aptyasya | gavām | janitrī | akṛta | pra | ketum |*
> *vi | ū~ iti | prathate | vitaram | varīyaḥ | ā | ubhā | pṛṇantī | pitroḥ | upasthā ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> अप्त्यस्य व्यापनशीलस्य विस्तृतस्य रजसो रञ्जकस्यान्तरिक्षलोकस्य । रजश्शब्दोऽन्तरिक्षलोकवाची लोका रजांस्युच्यन्त इति यास्कोक्तत्वात् । नि. ४-१९ । तस्य पूर्वेऽर्धे पूर्वस्मिन्भागे जनित्र्युत्पन्ना सती गवां दिशां रश्मीनां वा केतुं प्रज्ञानं प्राकृत । प्रकर्षेण करोति । यद्वा । रजसो रञ्जकस्याह्नः । रजश्शब्दोऽहर्वाची । अस्मिन्नहनि रजसी उच्येते इति यास्कोक्तत्वात् । नि. ४-१९ । तस्य पूर्वेऽर्धे पूर्वस्मिन्भागे उषःकाले गवां वाचां जनित्री जनयित्र्युत्पादयित्री । उषःकाले सर्वेषां प्राणिनां वाचः स्फुरन्तीति प्रसिद्धम् । यद्वा । अप्त्यस्य कर्मसु स्थितस्य जन्तोः केतुं गमनागमनादिरूपं कर्म । केतुरिति कर्मनाम केतः केतुरिति तन्नामसु पाठात् । प्राकृत । प्रकर्षेण करोति । किंच पित्रोः पालयित्र्योर्द्यावापृथिव्योरुपस्थे उत्सङ्गेऽन्तरालप्रदेशे स्थिता सती उभा उभे द्यावापृथिव्यौ पृणन्ती स्वतेजसा पूरयन्ती । यद्वा । उभोभयोः पित्रोरिति संबन्धः । वितरं विशिष्टतरं वरीय उरुतरमतिविस्तीर्णं यथा भवति तथा वि प्रथते । विशेषेणैव प्रख्याता भवति । प्रकाशत इत्यर्थः । उशब्दोऽवधारणार्थः पादपूरणो वा मिताक्षरेष्वनर्थकाः कमीमिद्धितीति यास्कोक्तत्वात् ॥

> *aptyasya vyāpanaśīlasya vistṛtasya rajaso rañjakasyāntarikṣalokasya | rajaśśabdo 'ntarikṣalokavācī lokā rajāṃsyucyanta iti yāskoktatvāt | ni. 4-19 | tasya pūrve 'rdhe pūrvasminbhāge janitryutpannā satī gavāṃ diśāṃ raśmīnāṃ vā ketuṃ prajñānaṃ prākṛta | prakarṣeṇa karoti | yadvā | rajaso rañjakasyāhnaḥ | rajaśśabdo 'harvācī | asminnahani rajasī ucyete iti yāskoktatvāt | ni. 4-19 | tasya pūrve 'rdhe pūrvasminbhāge uṣaḥkāle gavāṃ vācāṃ janitrī janayitryutpādayitrī | uṣaḥkāle sarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ vācaḥ sphurantīti prasiddham | yadvā | aptyasya karmasu sthitasya jantoḥ ketuṃ gamanāgamanādirūpaṃ karma | keturiti karmanāma ketaḥ keturiti tannāmasu pāṭhāt | prākṛta | prakarṣeṇa karoti | kiṃca pitroḥ pālayitryordyāvāpṛthivyorupasthe utsaṅge 'ntarālapradeśe sthitā satī ubhā ubhe dyāvāpṛthivyau pṛṇantī svatejasā pūrayantī | yadvā | ubhobhayoḥ pitroriti saṃbandhaḥ | vitaraṃ viśiṣṭataraṃ varīya urutaramativistīrṇaṃ yathā bhavati tathā vi prathate | viśeṣeṇaiva prakhyātā bhavati | prakāśata ityarthaḥ | uśabdo 'vadhāraṇārthaḥ pādapūraṇo vā mitākṣareṣvanarthakāḥ kamīmiddhitīti yāskoktatvāt ‖*

*(Read from the image; checked against the OCR, which is badly garbled here. The Nirukta references "4-19" are as printed "೪-೧೯" and as the OCR reads them.)* "Of *aptya* — the pervading, the extended — *rajas*, the colouring [world], the world of the atmosphere (the word *rajas* denotes the world of the atmosphere, since Yāska says '*lokā rajāṃsy ucyante*', Ni. 4-19); in its eastern half (*pūrve ardhe*), in the front part, being born (*janitrī*), she makes (*prākṛta*, 'makes excellently') a *ketu*, a knowledge (perception), of the *gavām* — of the quarters or of the rays. Or else of the *rajas*, the day which colours (the word *rajas* denotes the day, since Yāska says 'in this day the two worlds (*rajasī*) are spoken of', Ni. 4-19); in its eastern half, in the former part, at the time of Uṣas, she is the *janitrī* — the begetter, the producer — of *gavām* — voices (speeches); for it is well known that at the time of Uṣas the speech of all living beings comes to life. Or else, of the creature engaged in works (*aptya*), she makes the *ketu* — activity in the form of going and coming and so on (*ketu* is a name for 'action', since *ketaḥ*, *ketuḥ* are read among its names). Moreover, standing in the lap, the intermediate region, of *pitroḥ* — the two protecting parents, heaven and earth — *ubhā* — filling both heaven and earth with her own brilliance; or the construction is *ubhayoḥ pitroḥ*; she spreads out (*vi prathate*) more widely (*vitaram*), *variyaḥ* — most extensively, in the widest degree; she becomes known specially; that is, she shines. The word *u* is for emphasis, or a pāda-filler, as Yāska says 'among the measured syllables, *kam, īm, id, u* are meaningless' (Ni. 1-9)."

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *Aptyasya* — of the pervading; *rajasaḥ* — of the world of the atmosphere; *pūrve ardhe* — in the front part, at the time of Uṣas; *janitrī* — being born; *gavām* — of the quarters (the rays); *ketum* — the knowledge; *pra akṛta* — [Uṣas] makes abundantly (or): *aptyasya* — of the creature engaged in works; *rajasaḥ* — of the day; *pūrve ardhe* — in the first half; *gavām* — of voices; *janitrī* — as the mother; *ketum* — the knowledge of actions (going and coming and so on); *pra akṛta* — (the goddess Uṣas) makes well; (*kiṃca* — and); *pitroḥ* — of the two protecting parents, earth and sky; *upasthā* — in the lap region (being); *ubhā* — heaven and earth both; *ā pṛṇantī* — filling with her radiance; *vitaram* — more; *variyaḥ* — widely; *vi prathate* — becomes well known (shines).

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** Uṣas, being born in the front part of the pervading atmosphere (in the front part of the day), makes known the quarters (by her light). (Being born in the front part of the day, she gives the creature engaged in works the knowledge of its works, going and coming and so on;) and, shining between earth and sky — lighting up the two regions — she becomes still more widely known (shines).

*(The printed English translation of this ṛk begins at the foot of this page: "Born in the eastern" — see p. 153 below.)*

### Printed p. 153  (PDF 174)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 7.)*

**Printed English (Ṛk 5, as printed):** *Born in the eastern quarter of the spacious firmament, she displays a banner of rays of light. Placed on the lap of both parents (heaven and earth), filling them (with radiance), she enjoys vast and wide-spread renown.*

**Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 5.**

For the first half of this ṛk two kinds of meaning are stated. First: *aptyasya rajasaḥ pūrve ardhe janitrī gavāṃ ketuṃ pra akṛta* — in the front part (the first part) of the atmosphere, which is widely pervading, Uṣas is born and produces the knowledge of the ten quarters; second: *aptyasya* — for the creature engaged in works — *rajasaḥ* — of the day — *pūrve ardhe* — in the first half — *gavām* — of voices — *janitrī* — as the mother — *ketum* — the knowledge of actions — *pra akṛta* — she produces well. Therefore for the words *aptyasya* and the others both meanings must be given.

***aptyasya*** — *vyāpanaśīlasya vistṛtasya* — "very widely spread out": as an epithet of the atmosphere; or else, since the word *apas* is recorded among the names of *karman*, *aptyasya* means *karmasu sthitasya jantoḥ* — "of the creature engaged in the doing of work".

***rajasaḥ*** — *rajaśabdo 'ntarikṣalokavācī | lokā rajāṃsy ucyanta iti yāskoktatvāt* (Ni. 4-19, as printed "೪-೧೯") *tasya pūrve 'rdhe*. According to Yāska's opinion the word *rajas* means "atmosphere"; Sāyaṇa, giving this as the first meaning of the word, says "in the front part of such an atmosphere"; and second, *rajasaḥ rañjakasyāhnaḥ | rajaśabdo 'havācī | asyāhanī rajasī iti yāskoktatvāt* (4-19) *tasya pūrve 'rdhe* — since it is of the nature of colouring (*rañjana*), the day is named *rajas*; quoting Yāska's own sentence he has explained "of such *rajas*, i.e. of the day, in the first part". Thus the meanings are not only "atmosphere" and "day"; in some ṛks the word *rajas* is even explained as "water" —

> क्व स्विदस्य रजसो महस्परं क्वावरं मरुतो यस्मिन्नायय ।
> यच्च्यावयथ विथुरेव संहितं व्यद्रिणा पतथ त्वेषमर्णवम् ॥

> *kva svidasya rajaso mahasparaṃ kvāvaraṃ maruto yasminnāyaya |*
> *yaccyāvayatha vithureva saṃhitaṃ vyadriṇā patatha tveṣamarṇavam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-168-6, as read from the print; *vy adriṇā* as printed.)

***gavām*** — *diśāṃ raśmīnāṃ vā*: of the quarters, or of the rays — one meaning; or *gavāṃ vācāṃ janitrī* — "the mother of voices" — another meaning is stated. The word *go* is recorded in the Nirukta among words of many meanings. This is explained elsewhere.

### Printed p. 154  (PDF 175)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 18 Sū. 124".)*

***pitroḥ*** — *pālayitroḥ dyāvāpṛthivyoḥ*: "of the heaven and earth who are its protectors" — the heaven and earth are called the parents of Uṣas.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 5; noted briefly, numbers as read by the OCR).** *janitrī* — root *janī prādurbhāve*; the suffix *tṛc* [the print: *tṛn*] in the agent sense; *ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ* gives the augment *iṭ*; when the feminine is intended, *ṛnnebhyo ṅīp* gives ṅīp; *yaṇ* substitution; *ñnityādir nityam* (Pā. 6-1-197) gives the first-syllable acute. *akṛta* — root *ḍukṛñ karaṇe*; *chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ* (Pā. 3-4-6) gives luṅ in the present sense; as explained in the previous mantra, *luk* of *cli*; *nighāta* accent. *prathate* — root *prathaḥ prakhyāne*; laṭ third person singular; the *nighāta* accent. *vitaram* — root *tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ*; *pacādi aṭ* [*ac*]; guṇa with *raparatva*; final-acute by the suffix; in the compound the accent of the final member's own nature. *variyaḥ* — *atiśayena uru variyaḥ*; the suffix *īyasun* in the sense of excess; with it following, *priyasthirasphirorubahulagavyaprthucchandārasāṃ…* [print: *priyasthira-…-ror…*] (Pā. 6-4-157) gives *var* in place of *uru*; since the suffix is *nit* [as printed], *ñnityādir nityam* (Pā. 6-1-197) gives the first-syllable acute. *ubhā* — *supāṃ sulug…* (Pā. 7-1-39) gives *ā* to the case-ending (nominative dual, or genitive dual); likewise *ā* for the locative in *upasthā*. *pṛṇantī* — root *pṝ pālanapūraṇayoḥ*; Kryādi; śatṛ in the laṭ sense; *kryādibhyaḥ śnā*; since it belongs to the *prādi* group, *svādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ* shortens the root (Pā. 7-3-80); *śnābhyastayor ātaḥ* (Pā. 6-4-112) elides the *ā* of *śnā*; *ugitaś ca* gives ṅīp and *num* in the feminine; since a *ṛ*-vowel precedes, the *n* of the suffix becomes *ṇ*; the first-syllable acute of the śatṛ suffix. ‖ 5 ‖

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> एवेदेषा पुरुतमा दृशे कं नाजामिं न परि वृणक्ति जामिम् ।
> अरेपसा तन्वा शाशदाना नार्भादीषते न महो विभाती ॥ ६ ॥

> *evedeṣā purutamā dṛśe kaṃ nājāmiṃ na pari vṛṇakti jāmim |*
> *arepasā tanvā śāśadānā nārbhādīṣate na maho vibhātī ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> एव । इत् । एषा । पुरुऽतमा । दृशे । कम् । न । अजामिम् । न । परि । वृणक्ति । जामिम् ।
> अरेपसा । तन्वा । शाशदाना । न । अर्भात् । ईषते । न । महः । विऽभाती ॥ ६ ॥

> *eva | it | eṣā | puru 'tamā | dṛśe | kam | na | ajāmim | na | pari | vṛṇakti | jāmim |*
> *arepasā | tanvā | śāśadānā | na | arbhāt | īṣate | na | mahaḥ | vi 'bhātī ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> एषोषा एवेत् । इच्छब्द एवकारार्थः । एवमेवेदानींभासमानप्रकारेणैव पुरुतमा विपुलतमात्यन्तविस्तृता सत्यजामिं [?] विजातीयं मनुष्यादिजातिं न परि वृणक्ति । परितः सर्वतो न वर्जयति । तथा जामिं सजातीयं देवजातिं न परि वृणक्ति । न परिवर्जयति । मनुष्यादिकं देवादिकं च तदुपलक्षितं लोकद्वयं वा कात्स्न्र्येन प्रकाशयतीत्यर्थः । किमर्थमिति तदुच्यते । दृशे कं सुखेन सर्वेषां दर्शनाय । सुखं यथा भवति तथा सर्वान्दर्शयितुं वा । किंचारेपसापापया निर्मलया तन्वा शरीरेण शाशदाना शाशद्यमाना । शाशदानः शाशद्यमान इति यास्कः । नि. ६-१६ । स्पष्टतां गच्छन्तीत्यर्थः । विभाती विशेषेण प्रकाशयन्ती सार्भादल्पादपि वस्तुनः कस्मादपि सकाशान्नेषते । न गच्छति । तमसि प्रकाशयति । तथा महो महतो मेर्वादेः सकाशान्नेषते । न गच्छति । तमसि प्रकाशयति । पूर्वं लोकद्वयं प्रकाशत इत्युक्तम् । इदानीमस्मिँल्लोके परमाण्वादि पर्वतपर्यन्तं कृत्स्नं प्रकाशयतीत्यर्थः ॥

> *eṣoṣā evet | icchabda evakārārthaḥ | evamevedānīṃbhāsamānaprakāreṇaiva purutamā vipulatamātyantavistṛtā satyajāmiṃ [?] vijātīyaṃ manuṣyādijātiṃ na pari vṛṇakti | paritaḥ sarvato na varjayati | tathā jāmiṃ sajātīyaṃ devajātiṃ na pari vṛṇakti | na parivarjayati | manuṣyādikaṃ devādikaṃ ca tadupalakṣitaṃ lokadvayaṃ vā kātsnryena prakāśayatītyarthaḥ | kimarthamiti taducyate | dṛśe kaṃ sukhena sarveṣāṃ darśanāya | sukhaṃ yathā bhavati tathā sarvāndarśayituṃ vā | kiṃcārepasāpāpayā nirmalayā tanvā śarīreṇa śāśadānā śāśadyamānā | śāśadānaḥ śāśadyamāna iti yāskaḥ | ni. 6-16 | spaṣṭatāṃ gacchantītyarthaḥ | vibhātī viśeṣeṇa prakāśayantī sārbhādalpādapi vastunaḥ kasmādapi sakāśānneṣate | na gacchati | tamasi prakāśayati | tathā maho mahato mervādeḥ sakāśānneṣate | na gacchati | tamasi prakāśayati | pūrvaṃ lokadvayaṃ prakāśata ityuktam | idānīmasmi~lloke paramāṇvādi parvataparyantaṃ kṛtsnaṃ prakāśayatītyarthaḥ ‖*

*(Read from the image; checked against the OCR. The word "satyajāmiṃ" [?] near the beginning is as printed and doubtful, and several words in the second half are small in the print.)* "*Eṣā uṣāḥ eva it* — here *it* has the sense of *eva*. In just this way, as she now appears, *purutamā* — greatly extensive, spread out very widely — she does not exclude (*na pari vṛṇakti*, does not avoid on all sides) the *ajāmi*, the creatures of a different kind, men and the rest; likewise, the *jāmi*, those of her own kind, the race of the gods, she does not exclude; that is, she illumines entirely, men and the others and the gods and the others, or the two worlds characterized by them. What for? That is said: *dṛśe kam* — to be seen by all easily; or, so that all are seen, so that it is pleasant. Moreover with a faultless body (*arepasā*, free of sin, pure), *śāśadānā* — becoming visible ('*śāśadānaḥ* means *śāśadyamānaḥ*', says Yāska, Ni. 6-16), that is, going toward clarity. Shining specially (*vibhātī*), she does not go away from even a small thing (*arbhāt*), but lights it in the dark; and likewise from the great (*mahaḥ*), from Meru and the like, she does not go away: she lights it in the dark. It was said before that she shines on the two worlds; now, in this world, she lights up the whole, from an atom to a mountain: that is the sense."

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *Eṣā* — this Uṣas; *eva it* — in this very way; *purutamā* — most extensively spread out; *ajāmim* — those of a different kind, men and the rest (the world of men); *kaṃ dṛśe* — for easy seeing; *na pari vṛṇakti* — does not leave out; *jāmim* — those of her own kind, the gods; (the world of the gods); *na (pari vṛṇakti)* — does not leave out; *arepasā* — free of sin (pure); *tanvā* — with the body; *śāśadānā* — becoming visible; *vibhātī* — specially bright (Uṣas); *arbhāt* — from what is extremely small; *na īṣate* — does not go away; *mahaḥ* — from the very great; *na (īṣate)* — does not go away.

### Printed p. 156  (PDF 177)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 18 Sū. 124".)*

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** In this manner, spreading out extremely (widely), the Uṣas, leaving out neither the world of men (those of a different kind) nor the world of the gods (those of her own kind), becoming visible with a pure body, and having more light, illumines all objects, with no distinction of the small and the great.

**Printed English (as printed):** *Verily she, the wide-expanded Ushas, neglects not (to give) the joy of sight to those of her own or of a different nature : visible in her faultless person, and brightly shining, she passes not by the little or the great.*

**Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 6.**

***jāmiṃ ajāmim*** — for the word *jāmi* the meaning "gods of the same kind", and for *ajāmi* the meaning "humans and others of a different kind", is given. For the word *jāmi* the author of the Nirukta says: *jāmir anyasyāṃ janayanti jāmy apatyam | jamater vā syād gatikarmaṇo nirgamanaprāyā bhavati* (Ni. 3-6, as printed "೩-೬"). One derivation of *jāmi* is from the root *jan*, which gives the meaning "to be born", expressing the intention that "another helps her to produce children"; another derivation is from the root *jam*, meaning "to go", expressing that "she is one who goes to the house of her husband". By these two explanations it is known from the Nirukta explanation that the word *jāmi* means "sister". In support of this meaning —

> न जामये तान्वो रिक्थमारैक्चकार गर्भं सनितुर्निधानम् ।
> यदी मातरो जनयन्त वह्निमन्यः कर्ता सुकृतोरन्य ऋन्धन् ॥

> *na jāmaye tānvo rikthamāraikcakāra garbhaṃ saniturnidhānam |*
> *yadī mātaro janayanta vahnimanyaḥ kartā sukṛtoranya ṛndhan ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-31-2, as read from the print "೩-೩೧-೨".) *(Read letter by letter; "rikthamāraik" is as printed and doubtful.)* — citing this ṛk, the word *jāmi* is explained as "sister". Likewise, as explained in the preceding sūkta in this section,

### Printed p. 157  (PDF 178)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 7.)*

> भगस्य स्वसा वरुणस्य जामिरुषः सूनृते प्रथमा जरस्व ।
> पश्चा स दध्या यो अघस्य धाता जयेम तं दक्षिणया रथेन ॥

> *bhagasya svasā varuṇasya jāmiruṣaḥ sūnṛte prathamā jarasva |*
> *paścā sa dadhyā yo aghasya dhātā jayema taṃ dakṣiṇayā rathena ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-123-5, as printed "೧-೧೨೩-೫".) — in this and other ṛks too the meaning "sister" is the sense of the word *jāmi*.

But in the present ṛk the meaning of this word comes out in a wider extent, as "kinsmen". *Jāmiṃ ajāmim* — the gods who are kinsmen, and men and the rest who are not kinsmen: that is the meaning. In the same way the extended sense "kinsmen":

> जामिः सिन्धूनां भ्रातेव स्वस्रामिभ्यान्न राजा वनान्यत्ति ।
> यद्वातजूतो वना व्यस्थादग्निर्ह दाति रोमा पृथिव्याः ॥

> *jāmiḥ sindhūnāṃ bhrāteva svasrāmibhyānna rājā vanānyatti |*
> *yadvātajūto vanā vyasthādagnirha dāti romā pṛthivyāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-65-4, as read from the print.)

> कस्ते जामिर्जनानामग्ने को दाश्वध्वरः । को ह कस्मिन्नसि श्रितः ॥

> *kaste jāmirjanānāmagne ko dāśvadhvaraḥ | ko ha kasminnasi śritaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-75-3, as read from the print.) — in these and other ṛks the meaning "kinsmen" is given just as in this ṛk.

***na parivṛṇakti*** — *na parivarjayati | manuṣyādikaṃ devādikaṃ ca tadupalakṣitaṃ lokadvayaṃ vā kārtsnyena prakāśayatīty arthaḥ*: she illumines the two worlds that are filled with gods, men and others, without making a distinction — that is the meaning.

***arepasā*** — *apāpayā nirmalayā tanvā*: "with a body free of sin", that is, with a pure body. The author of the Nirukta, citing

> इदेह जाता समवावशीतामरेपसा तन्वा नामभिः स्वैः ।
> जिष्णुर्वामन्यः सुमखस्य सूरिर्दिवो अन्यः सुभगः पुत्र ऊहे ॥

> *ideha jātā samavāvaśītāmarepasā tanvā nāmabhiḥ svaiḥ |*
> *jiṣṇurvāmanyaḥ sumakhasya sūrirdivo anyaḥ subhagaḥ putra ūhe ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-181-4 [?], as I read the print.) — as the words *arepasā tanvā* in it are explained as "with a body not touched by sin", so it is to be said here too.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 6, pp. 157–158; noted briefly, numbers as read by the OCR).** *purutamā* — suffix *tamap* in the sense of excess; in the feminine, *ṭāp*, taking the stem ending in *a* as its cause. *dṛśe* — root *dṛśir prekṣaṇe*; *dṛśe vikhye ca* (Pā. 3-4-11) records it as *dṛśe*; since it ends in *e*, it becomes an indeclinable.

### Printed p. 158  (PDF 179)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 18 Sū. 124".)*

*ajāmim* — *na jāmiḥ ajāmiḥ tam*; *tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyā…* (Pā. 6-2-2) gives the natural accent of the first member, the negative *nañ*; accusative singular. *vṛṇakti* — root *vṛjī varjane*; Rudhādi; laṭ third person singular *tip*; *rudhādibhyaḥ śnam* (Pā. 3-1-78) gives *śnam*; *midaco 'ntyāt paraḥ* places it after the last vowel; *coḥ kuḥ* gives the guttural for the *j* of the root, and *car*; since a *ṛ* precedes, the *n* becomes *ṇ*; since it follows a non-verb word, the *nighāta* accent. *arepasā* — *na vidyate repaḥ yasyāḥ sā arepāḥ tayā arepasā*; *nañsubhyām* (Pā. 6-2-172) gives the final-acute of the latter member. *tanvā* — with the instrumental singular following, *tanvādīnāṃ chandasy upasaṃkhyānam* gives *yaṇ*; the *yaṇ* stands in the place of the acute; the case-ending follows it; *udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svaritaḥ* (Pā. 8-2-4) gives the *svarita*. *śāśadānā* — explained in Ṛk 10 of 1-123; only the nasalisation (*anunāsikatva*) does not occur here. *īṣate* — root *īṣa gatihiṃsādarśaneṣu*; Bhvādi; laṭ third person singular *īṣate*; since the *sārvadhātuka* follows the *upadeśa*, *tāsyanudāttet* (Pā. 6-1-186) makes it unaccented, and since *śap* is *pit* the root-accent remains. *mahaḥ* — *mahataḥ*, with the loss of the *t* in the Veda; or else the root *maha pūjāyām*, with *kvip* (*kvip ca*); ablative singular; *sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ* (Pā. 6-1-168) gives the acute to the case-ending. *vibhātī* — root *bhā dīptau*; śatṛ in the laṭ sense; *ugitaś ca* (Pā. 4-1-6) gives ṅīp in the feminine; since ṅīp follows a śatṛ without *num*, *śatur anumo nadyajādī* (Pā. 6-1-173) gives it the acute accent; in the compound the accent of the final member. ‖ 6 ‖

#### Ṛk 7

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अभ्रातेव पुंस एति प्रतीची गर्तारुगिव सनये धनानाम् ।
> जायेव पत्य उशती सुवासा उषा हस्रेव नि रिणीते अप्सः ॥ ७ ॥

> *abhrāteva puṃsa eti pratīcī gartārugiva sanaye dhanānām |*
> *jāyeva patya uśatī suvāsā uṣā hasreva ni riṇīte apsaḥ ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अभ्रातीऽइव । पुंसः । एति । प्रतीची । गर्तऽआरुक्ऽइव । सनये । धनानाम् ।
> जायाऽइव । पत्ये । उशती । सुऽवासाः । उषाः । हस्राऽइव । नि । रिणीते । अप्सः ॥ ७ ॥

> *abhrātī 'iva | puṃsaḥ | eti | pratīcī | garta 'āruk 'iva | sanaye | dhanānām |*
> *jāyā 'iva | patye | uśatī | su 'vāsāḥ | uṣāḥ | hasrā 'iva | ni | riṇīte | apsaḥ ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> अभ्रातेव भ्रातृरहितेव पुंसः पित्रादीन्प्रति प्रतीची स्वकीयस्थानात्प्रतिनिवृत्तमुखी सती एति । गच्छति । यथा लोके भ्रातृरहिता योषित्स्वोचितवासोऽलंकारादिलाभाय पित्र्यं गेहं [?] सति भ्रातरि स निवोचितप्रदानादिना सम्यक् तोषयति । तदभावाप्तिकरमेव प्राप्नोति । यद्वा । सति स्वभ्रातरि स एव पितुः पिण्डदानादिकं सन्तानकृत्यं करोति । तस्याभावात्सैवेयमेव तत्कर्तुं पित्रादीन्गच्छति । तद्वदियमुषा अपि स्वोचितप्रकाशादिलाभाय स्वप्रकाशदानाय वा पित्रैव भूतं सूर्यमाभिमुख्येन गच्छति । अयमेको दृष्टान्तः । तथा धनानां सनये गर्तारुगिवेत्यपरो दृष्टान्तः । गर्त इति गृहनाम कृदरो गर्त इति तन्नामसु पाठात् । अत्रापीति [?] राजपुरुषैर्न्यायनिर्णेतृभिर्यध्यधिष्ठितं [?] स्थानमुच्यते । तदारोहतीति गर्तारुक् । यथा लोके काचिद्गतभर्तृका योषित्स्वानां स्वकीयैरिक्थानां सनये लाभाय गर्तमागच्छति । तां तु सभ्या विचार्य यदीयं रिक्थं लभते चेदेष्वस्मै संताड्य [?] तदीयं धनं वितरन्ति । तथेयमपि धनानां प्रीतिसाधनानां प्रकाशानां सनये लाभाय गर्तमाकाशं सूर्यनिवासस्थानमारोहति । देशविशेषाचारमपेक्ष्यैवं दृष्टान्तितम् । किंच पत्ये उशती कामयमाना सुवासा जायेव । अयमुषसो दृष्टान्तः । यथा च लोके सुवासा दुकूलादिशोभनवसना स्वलंकृता पूर्वं रजोदर्शनसमये मलिनवस्त्रा सती स्नानानन्तरं शोभनवस्त्राभरणादिना शोभमाना विशेषेण

> *abhrāteva bhrātṛrahiteva puṃsaḥ pitrādīnprati pratīcī svakīyasthānātpratinivṛttamukhī satī eti | gacchati | yathā loke bhrātṛrahitā yoṣitsvocitavāso 'laṃkārādilābhāya pitryaṃ gehaṃ [?] sati bhrātari sa nivocitapradānādinā samyak toṣayati | tadabhāvāptikarameva prāpnoti | yadvā | sati svabhrātari sa eva pituḥ piṇḍadānādikaṃ santānakṛtyaṃ karoti | tasyābhāvātsaiveyameva tatkartuṃ pitrādīngacchati | tadvadiyamuṣā api svocitaprakāśādilābhāya svaprakāśadānāya vā pitraiva bhūtaṃ sūryamābhimukhyena gacchati | ayameko dṛṣṭāntaḥ | tathā dhanānāṃ sanaye gartārugivetyaparo dṛṣṭāntaḥ | garta iti gṛhanāma kṛdaro garta iti tannāmasu pāṭhāt | atrāpīti [?] rājapuruṣairnyāyanirṇetṛbhiryadhyadhiṣṭhitaṃ [?] sthānamucyate | tadārohatīti gartāruk | yathā loke kācidgatabhartṛkā yoṣitsvānāṃ svakīyairikthānāṃ sanaye lābhāya gartamāgacchati | tāṃ tu sabhyā vicārya yadīyaṃ rikthaṃ labhate cedeṣvasmai saṃtāḍya [?] tadīyaṃ dhanaṃ vitaranti | tatheyamapi dhanānāṃ prītisādhanānāṃ prakāśānāṃ sanaye lābhāya gartamākāśaṃ sūryanivāsasthānamārohati | deśaviśeṣācāramapekṣyaivaṃ dṛṣṭāntitam | kiṃca patye uśatī kāmayamānā suvāsā jāyeva | ayamuṣaso dṛṣṭāntaḥ | yathā ca loke suvāsā dukūlādiśobhanavasanā svalaṃkṛtā pūrvaṃ rajodarśanasamaye malinavastrā satī snānānantaraṃ śobhanavastrābharaṇādinā śobhamānā viśeṣeṇa*
