## Sūkta 126 — *amandān stomān* (begins on printed p. 219)

**ನೂರ ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತಾರನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು — Nūra ippattāraneya sūktavu** (the one hundred and twenty-sixth Sūkta).

**॥ भूमिका ॥ — Introduction (Sanskrit, from the Sāyaṇa text):**

> अमन्दानिति षष्ठं सूक्तं सप्तेत्यनुवर्तमानात्सप्तर्चम् । आदितः पञ्चानां कक्षीवानृषिः षष्ठ्या भावयव्यः सप्तम्या रोमशा नाम ब्रह्मवादिनी । आदितः पञ्चानां भावयव्यस्य स्तुतिरूपत्वात्स एव देवता यातेनोच्यते [?] । अनु. २-५ [?] । इति न्यायात् । अन्त्ययोः षष्ठीसप्तम्योः स्वभाव्ययो रोमशयोः संवादः । षष्ठ्या भावयव्यः सप्तम्या रोमशा । यद्यपि स्वनयेन दत्ता इति श्रूयमाणत्वात्तस्य स्तुत्या भाव्यं तथापि पितृपुत्रयोरभेदात् आ रुद्रास इतिवत् पित्रैव नाम्ना व्यवहर्तुम् [?] । प्रथमाद्यानुष्टुब्वैत्यत्र [?] भाव्यस्येत्युक्तत्वाच्च भावयव्यं तुष्टावेत्यादिविरुद्धम् [?] उक्तं [?] पूर्वसूक्ते एव । आदितः पञ्च त्रिष्टुभः । अन्त्ये अनुष्टुभौ । तथा चानुक्रान्तम् । अमन्दानिति कक्षीवान्दानतुष्टः पञ्चभिर्भावयव्यं तुष्टावान्त्ये अनुष्टुभौ भावयव्यरोमशयोर्दम्पत्योः संवाद इति ॥ उक्तो विनियोगः ॥

> *amandāniti ṣaṣṭhaṃ sūktaṃ saptetyanuvartamānātsaptarcam | āditaḥ pañcānāṃ kakṣīvānṛṣiḥ ṣaṣṭhyā bhāvayavyaḥ saptamyā romaśā nāma brahmavādinī | āditaḥ pañcānāṃ bhāvayavyasya stutirūpatvātsa eva devatā yātenocyate [?] | anu. 2-5 [?] | iti nyāyāt | antyayoḥ ṣaṣṭhīsaptamyoḥ svabhāvyayo romaśayoḥ saṃvādaḥ | ṣaṣṭhyā bhāvayavyaḥ saptamyā romaśā | yadyapi svanayena dattā iti śrūyamāṇatvāttasya stutyā bhāvyaṃ tathāpi pitṛputrayorabhedāt ā rudrāsa itivat pitraiva nāmnā vyavahartum [?] | prathamādyānuṣṭubvaityatra [?] bhāvyasyetyuktatvācca bhāvayavyaṃ tuṣṭāvetyādiviruddham [?] uktaṃ [?] pūrvasūkte eva | āditaḥ pañca triṣṭubhaḥ | antye anuṣṭubhau | tathā cānukrāntam | amandāniti kakṣīvāndānatuṣṭaḥ pañcabhirbhāvayavyaṃ tuṣṭāvāntye anuṣṭubhau bhāvayavyaromaśayordampatyoḥ saṃvāda iti ‖ ukto viniyogaḥ ‖*

*(Read from the image; the middle sentences are in small type and several words — marked [?] — are doubtful; the OCR's Devanagari is badly garbled there. The Anukramaṇī sentence at the end is clear to me.)* "*Amandān* — the sixth sūkta, of seven ṛks (by the continuing 'seven'). Of the first five the ṛṣi is Kakṣīvān; of the sixth, Bhāvayavya; of the seventh, Romaśā, a *brahmavādinī*. Since the first five are in praise of Bhāvayavya, he is the deity, by the rule *yā tenocyate sā devatā* (Anu. 2-5 [?]). In the last two, the sixth and the seventh, there is a dialogue between the husband Bhāvayavya and Romaśā; the sixth is Bhāvayavya's, the seventh Romaśā's. … The first five are Triṣṭubh; the last two Anuṣṭubh. So the Anukramaṇī says: '*Amandān* — Kakṣīvān, pleased with the gift, praised Bhāvayavya in five; the last two, Anuṣṭubh, a dialogue between the married pair Bhāvayavya and Romaśā.' The *viniyoga* has been stated [before]."

*Reference numbers printed on this page as read by the reader's Google-Docs OCR (digits only; hyphens and sometimes a digit may be lost — use only as a check):* 3-3-92; 6-4-64; 6-2-139; 6-2-2; 3-5; 2-5

### Printed p. 220  (PDF 241)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 18 Sū. 126".)*

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** This Sūkta, beginning *amandān*, is the sixth Sūkta in the eighteenth Anuvāka. It has seven ṛks. In this Sūkta the ṛṣi of the first five ṛks is Kakṣīvān; of the sixth ṛk, Bhāvayavya; of the seventh, a *brahmavādinī* named Romaśā. Since the first five ṛks contain praise of Bhāvayavya, by the rule of the Anukramaṇī *sa eva devatā yā tenocyate* (Anu. 2-5) that praise is the deity; and since the sixth and seventh ṛks contain a conversation between Bhāvayavya and Romaśā, the deities of the sixth ṛk are Romaśā and of the seventh Bhāvayavya. But since in the third ṛk of the previous Sūkta it is said *svanayena dattāḥ*, a doubt arises that the praise may be of Svanaya; yet, as in the custom where the Maruts, sons of Rudra, are addressed by the name of their father *rudrāsaḥ*, so here too it is natural to use for the son the name of the father, Bhāvayavya, though Svanaya is the name of the son. Besides, since in the first ṛk the name Bhāvayavya is clearly stated, it must be understood that in this sūkta the ṛṣi praises Bhāvayavya. Thus the mutual contradiction is removed; this was said earlier in the preceding sūkta. The first five ṛks of this Sūkta are in Triṣṭubh metre, and the last two in Anuṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: *amandāniti kakṣīvān dānatuṣṭaḥ pañcabhir bhāvayavyaṃ tuṣṭāvānuṣṭubhau bhāvayavyaromaśayor dampatyoḥ saṃvāda*. The viniyoga was stated before.

**सूक्त—१२६ — Sūkta 126**

मण्डल—१ ‖ अनुवाक—१८ ‖ सूक्त—१२६ ‖ अष्टक—२ ‖ अध्याय—१ ‖ वर्ग—११ ‖ (as read; the print shows "೧೧" after "ವರ್ಗ".)

Number of ṛks in this Sūkta — 7. Ṛṣi — 1–5 Kakṣīvān Dairghatamasa Auśija; 6 Bhāvayavya; 7 Romaśā. Devatā — 1–5 Bhāvayavya (as printed "ಭಾವ್ಯಸ್ಯ"? — read as Bhāvayavya's praise); 6 Romaśā; 7 Bhāvayavya. Chandas — 1–5 Triṣṭubh; 6–7 Anuṣṭubh.

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अमन्दान्त्स्तोमान्प्र भरे मनीषा सिन्धावधि क्षियतो भाव्यस्य ।

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 11.)*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अमन्दान् । स्तोमान् । प्र । भरे । मनीषा । सिन्धौ । अधि । क्षियतः । भाव्यस्य ।
> यः । मे । सहस्रम् । अमिमीत । सवान् । अतूर्तः । राजा । श्रवः । इच्छमानः ॥ १ ॥

> *amandān | stomān | pra | bhare | manīṣā | sindhau | adhi | kṣiyataḥ | bhāvyasya |*
> *yaḥ | me | sahasram | amimīta | savān | atūrtaḥ | rājā | śravaḥ | icchamānaḥ ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> सिन्धौ सिन्धुदेशे यद्वा लक्षणया सिन्धुतीरे समुद्रतीरेऽधि क्षियतोऽधिनिवसतो भाव्यस्य भावयव्यस्य । तत्पुत्रस्य स्वनयस्येत्यर्थः । तस्मा अमन्दानल्पान् स्तोमान् स्तोत्राणि तन्निष्ठबहुविधदानादीनां कीर्तनानि मनीषा मनीषया प्रियातिशयबुद्ध्या प्र भरे प्रकर्षेण संपादयामि । कस्य विशेष इति तत्राह । अतूर्तः केनाप्यहिंसितो यो राजा मे मदर्थं सहस्रं तत्संख्याकान्सवान् । सूयन्ते सोमा एत इति सवाः सोमयागाः । तानमिमीत संपूर्णधनप्रदानेन निर्मितवान् [?] । किमिच्छन् । श्रवः सर्वैः श्रूयमाणां कीर्तिमात्मन इच्छमानः कामयमानः । यतोऽयमार्त्विज्यादुपाधिना विना कीर्त्यर्थमेव बहु धनं प्रादात् अतस्तं स्तौमीत्यर्थः ॥

*(Read from the image; checked against the OCR, which agrees on the structure. The word "nirmitavān" [?] near the end of the middle sentence is doubtful.)* "*Sindhau* — in the Sindhu country, or, by implication, on the bank of the Sindhu, on the sea-shore; *adhi kṣiyataḥ* — of *bhāvyasya*, Bhāvayavya, dwelling there; that is, of his son Svanaya. For him I *pra bhare* — bring forth well, compose — *amandān stomān* — not small praises, songs of praise, proclamations of his many gifts and the like — *manīṣā*, with the mind, with a mind exceedingly fond. Who is the particular one? To that he says: *atūrtaḥ* — unharmed by anyone — *yaḥ rājā* — the king who for my sake *sahasram savān* — a thousand Soma sacrifices (*savāḥ* are the Soma sacrifices, since 'these Soma are pressed') — *amimīta* — built, by the bestowal of full wealth. Wishing what? *Śravaḥ* — fame that is heard of by all, desiring it for himself. Since he gave much wealth for fame alone, without the pretext of priestly service, therefore I praise him: that is the sense."

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *Atūrtaḥ* — unharmed; *yaḥ rājā* — the king (called Svanaya); *me* — for me; *sahasram* — a thousand; *savān* — (Soma) sacrifices; *śravaḥ* — (only) fame; *icchamānaḥ* — wishing; *amimīta* — (by giving wealth) has made; *tasya* — that [king]; *sindhau* — on the bank of the Sindhu (sea); *adhi kṣiyataḥ* — dwelling; *bhāvyasya* — of Bhāvayavya's son Svanaya; *amandān* — endless; *stomān* — praises; *manīṣā* — with a mind; *pra bhare* — I make (I praise).

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** (Having given wealth for the performance of a thousand Soma sacrifices, he made [the sacrifices] favourable to me, out of desire for fame alone;) I praise with my mind that king called Svanaya, son of Bhāvayavya, who dwells on the sea-shore.

### Printed p. 222  (PDF 243)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 18 Sū. 126".)*

**Printed English (as printed):** *I repeat with a (willing) mind, the unreluctant praises of Bhavya, dwelling on the banks of the Sindhu : a prince of unequalled (might), desirous of renown, who has enabled me to celebrate a thousand sacrifices.*

**Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 1.**

***amandān stomān*** — *analpān kīrtanāni*: "not small, many praises". It is stated that "I resolve to compose praises in the form of Soma, which are not small and are of many kinds". In the present ṛk, though *stoma* means "praise", we shall consider carefully the descriptions of the various *stomas* as they apply.

Among the *stomas* there are nine main divisions: the *trivṛt* stoma, the *pañcadaśa* stoma, the *saptadaśa* stoma, the *ekaviṃśa* stoma, the *triṇava* stoma, the *trayastriṃśa* stoma, the *caturviṃśa* stoma, the *catuścatvāriṃśa* stoma, and the *aṣṭācatvāriṃśa* stoma; and the numbers of ṛks are in accordance with the name of each stoma. This number is to be understood as applying to each *viṣṭuti* of the stoma. Their descriptions are given at length in the 2nd part of the Ṛk Saṃhitā, pp. 139 to 19[?] [as printed; the second numeral is not clear to me].

Of these stomas, the *trivṛt* stoma is recited at the morning pressing, the *pañcadaśa* at the midday pressing, and the *saptadaśa* at the third pressing. In sacrifices such as the *abhiplava ṣaḍaha*, after the singing of the stomas — *trivṛt* and the like — which must be sung in the rites such as the morning pressing, there are other stomas, said in some contexts to be *uttara-stomas*, whose singing is called *stomavṛddhi* ("increase of the stoma"). For the singing of these increases of the stoma, ṛks of a larger number are to be recited, in order to equal the increase, by the *maitrāvaruṇa*, *brāhmaṇācchaṃsin* and *acchāvāka* priests of the *hotṛ* group.

Thus the nine divisions stated above can also be increased by *āvāpa* (insertion) to thirteen, fourteen, sixteen and so on. For example —

> वसवस्त्रयोदशाक्षरेण त्रयोदशं स्तोममुदजयन्रुद्राश्चतुर्दशाक्षरेण चतुर्दशग्ं स्तोममुदजयन्नादित्याः पञ्चदशाक्षरेण पञ्चदशग्ं स्तोममुदजयन्नदितिः षोडशाक्षरेण षोडशग्ं स्तोममुदजयत्प्रजापतिः सप्तदशाक्षरेण सप्तदशग्ं स्तोममुदजयत् ॥

> *vasavastrayodaśākṣareṇa trayodaśaṃ stomamudajayanrudrāścaturdaśākṣareṇa caturdaśagṃ stomamudajayannādityāḥ pañcadaśākṣareṇa pañcadaśagṃ stomamudajayannaditiḥ ṣoḍaśākṣareṇa ṣoḍaśagṃ stomamudajayatprajāpatiḥ saptadaśākṣareṇa saptadaśagṃ stomamudajayat ‖*

(Tai. Saṃ. 1-2-11-? [?], as read — the numerals "೧-೨-೧೧-೪೪" are small and doubtful.) *(Read letter by letter; the *ग्ं* notation is as printed.)* "The Vasus, with a thirteen-syllable [formula], won the thirteenfold stoma; the Rudras, with a fourteen-syllable, won the fourteenfold stoma; the Ādityas with a fifteen-syllable won the fifteenfold stoma; Aditi with a sixteen-syllable won the sixteenfold stoma; Prajāpati with a seventeen-syllable won the seventeenfold stoma" — by these Taittirīya Saṃhitā sentences the order in which the Vasus, Rudras, Ādityas, Aditi and Prajāpati won the thirteen-, fourteen-, fifteen-, sixteen-, and seventeen-fold stomas is

> प्रातःसवने वै गायत्रेण छन्दसा त्रिवृते स्तोमाय ज्योतिर्दधदेति त्रिवृता ब्रह्मवर्चसेन पञ्चदशाय ज्योतिर्दधदेति पञ्चदशेनौजसा वीर्येण सप्तदशाय ज्योतिर्दधदेति सप्तदशेन प्राजापत्येन प्रजननेनैकविंशाय ज्योतिर्दधदेति स्तोम एव तत्स्तोमाय ज्योतिर्दधदेत्यथो स्तोम एव स्तोममभि प्रणयति यावन्तो वै स्तोमास्तावन्तः कामास्तावन्तो लोकास्तावन्ति ज्योतींषि तावत एव स्तोमानेतावतः कामानेतावतो लोकानेतावन्ति ज्योतींष्यवरुन्धे ॥

> *prātaḥsavane vai gāyatreṇa chandasā trivṛte stomāya jyotirdadhadeti trivṛtā brahmavarcasena pañcadaśāya jyotirdadhadeti pañcadaśenaujasā vīryeṇa saptadaśāya jyotirdadhadeti saptadaśena prājāpatyena prajananenaikaviṃśāya jyotirdadhadeti stoma eva tatstomāya jyotirdadhadetyatho stoma eva stomamabhi praṇayati yāvanto vai stomāstāvantaḥ kāmāstāvanto lokāstāvanti jyotīṃṣi tāvata eva stomānetāvataḥ kāmānetāvato lokānetāvanti jyotīṃṣyavarundhe ‖*

(Tai. Saṃ. 2-1-3-2 [?], as read; the numerals are small and doubtful.) *(Read letter by letter from the print; a few syllables of the second half are doubtful — "ekaviṃśāya" and "pra-ṇayati" are as printed.)* "In the morning pressing, with the gāyatra metre, he goes bringing light for the *trivṛt* stoma, with the *trivṛt* [which is] *brahmavarcasa*; he goes bringing light for the fifteenfold, with the fifteenfold [which is] vigour, heroism; for the seventeenfold, with the seventeenfold [which is] of Prajāpati, procreation; for the twenty-one-fold, … the stoma indeed, he leads the stoma to the stoma. As many as are the stomas, so many are the desires, so many the worlds, so many the lights: so many stomas, so many desires, so many worlds, so many lights he wins." In these sentences the power of four kinds of stoma is stated. The sacrificer, at the morning pressing, sets the *trivṛt* stoma, with the gāyatra metre, in a place of eminence; likewise with the *trivṛt* he makes the *pañcadaśa* stoma shine like a light; and the fifteenfold [he makes] full of heroism; and, with the seventeenfold, which has connection with Prajāpati and is the means of procreation, he makes the twenty-one-fold full of splendour. Thus one kind of stoma gives power and brilliance to another. As many as the stomas there are, so many worlds, so many brilliances, so many desired ends; and one who recites the stomas wins so many: thus the power of the stomas is explained, and then the loss that follows from non-recitation of the stomas.

> यजते यो वै स्तोमानामवमं परमतां गच्छन्तं वेद परमतामेव गच्छति त्रिवृद्वै स्तोमानामवमस्त्रिवृत्परमो य एवं वेद परमतामेव गच्छति ॥

> *yajate yo vai stomānāmavamaṃ paramatāṃ gacchantaṃ veda paramatāmeva gacchati trivṛdvai stomānāmavamastrivṛtparamo ya evaṃ veda paramatāmeva gacchati ‖*

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-1-3-8 to 10 [?], as read from the OCR "६-१-३-८ रिंद १०"; the print "೬-೧-೩-೮" is small.) The scholars of the śāstra have laid down that one who sacrifices with the Agniṣṭoma must sacrifice with all stomas. In this rule, if the *trivṛt* stoma is left out, his vital breaths are lost, so the sacrificer sacrifices with the thought "let this sacrifice be contained in my vital breaths"; likewise if the *pañcadaśa* is left out, heroic strength is lost; if the *saptadaśa* is left out, he goes without progeny; if the *ekaviṃśa* is left out, his support (*pratiṣṭhā*) is lost; if the *triṇava* is left out, … the seasons and the stars (as helpers) are lost to him; if the *trayastriṃśa* is left out, the chief deities are lost: so the sacrificer performs the rite by *pañcadaśa* for the sake of heroic strength, by *saptadaśa* for the gain of progeny, by *ekaviṃśa* for the support of life, by *triṇava* for the benefit of the seasons and constellations, by *trayastriṃśa* for the gain of the deities. He who knows the greatness of the *trivṛt* stoma, which has the first place among all stomas, wins the first place among sacrificers.

Thus describing the glory of the *trivṛt* and other stomas —

> त्रिवृदग्निष्टोमो भवति तेज एवावरुन्धे पञ्चदशो भवतीन्द्रियमेवावरुन्धे सप्तदशो भवत्यन्नाद्यमवरुन्धे । अथो एकविंशो भवति प्रतिष्ठित्यै । अथो रुचमेवात्मन्धत्ते त्रिणवो भवति विजित्यै त्रयस्त्रिंशो भवति प्रतिष्ठित्यै ॥

> *trivṛdagniṣṭomo bhavati teja evāvarundhe pañcadaśo bhavatīndriyamevāvarundhe saptadaśo bhavatyannādyamavarundhe | atho ekaviṃśo bhavati pratiṣṭhityai | atho rucamevātmandhatte triṇavo bhavati vijityai trayastriṃśo bhavati pratiṣṭhityai ‖*

(Tai. Saṃ. 2-1-3-3 [?], as read; "ekaviṃśa … pratiṣṭhityai" is as printed and the clause order is doubtful in my reading.) *(Read letter by letter; marked doubtful as a whole, since the passage is small and the OCR garbles it.)* — by the *trivṛt* stoma he wins brilliance; by the fifteenfold, vigour; by the seventeenfold, food; by the twenty-one-fold, support; by the *triṇava*, victory; by the thirty-three-fold, greatness: thus the purposes of reciting the stomas are told. Also in the Kaṭha Upaniṣad —

> *yena chandasā stoṣyansyāttacchanda upadhāvedyena stomena stoṣyamāṇaḥ syāttaṃ stomamupadhāvet |*

(Chā. U. [as printed "ಛಾ. ಉ. ೧-೩-೧೦" read from the print; the OCR reads "१-३-१०"].) — by this sentence the greatness of the *udgītha* is described, and it is ordained that one should resort to the stoma by which the praise suits that context and is brought to completion, and meditate on it.

In the same way in the present ṛk also, from the word *stomān* the sense is "praise (*stotra*) that is of the nature of song, of the nature of eulogy, and of surpassing usefulness". The author of the Nirukta has explained this ṛk as follows:

> अमन्दान्स्तोमान्प्र भरे मनीषा अमन्दानल्पान्वा । बालो बलवर्ती भर्तव्यो भवत्यम्बास्मा अलं भवतीति वाम्बा बलं भवतीति वा बलो वा प्रतिषेद्धव्यव्यवहितः [?] । प्रभरे मनीषया मनसा ईषया स्तुत्या प्रज्ञया वा । सिन्धावधि निवसतो भावयव्यस्य राज्ञः । यो मे सहस्रं निरमिमीत सवानतूर्तो राजातर्ण इति वात्वरमाण इति वा प्रशंसामिच्छमानः ॥

> *amandānstomānpra bhare manīṣā amandānalpānvā | bālo balavartī bhartavyo bhavatyambāsmā alaṃ bhavatīti vāmbā balaṃ bhavatīti vā balo vā pratiṣeddhavyavyavahitaḥ [?] | prabhare manīṣayā manasā īṣayā stutyā prajñayā vā | sindhāvadhi nivasato bhāvayavyasya rājñaḥ | yo me sahasraṃ niramimīta savānatūrto rājātarṇa iti vātvaramāṇa iti vā praśaṃsāmicchamānaḥ ‖*

> सविता यन्त्रैः पृथिवीमरम्णादस्कम्भने सविता द्यामदृंहत् ।
> अश्वमिवाधुक्षद्धुनिमन्तरिक्षमतूर्ते बद्धं सविता समुद्रम् ॥

> *savitā yantraiḥ pṛthivīmaramṇādaskambhane savitā dyāmadṛṃhat |*
> *aśvamivādhukṣaddhunimantarikṣamatūrte baddhaṃ savitā samudram ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-149-1, as read from the print "೧೦-೧೪೯-೧".) (Ni. 10-32 [?], as read), says in that ṛk too the same meaning *ātūrṇa iti vā tvaramāṇa iti vā*. Here two qualities of Bhāvayavya (Svanaya) appear: first, because he has surpassing prowess he is one who cannot be conquered or harmed by anyone; second, because he is wise, he is one whose conduct is without haste, full of discrimination.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 1; noted briefly, numbers as read by the OCR).** *amandān* — *na mandāḥ amandāḥ tān amandān*; *tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyā…* (Pā. 6-2-2) gives the natural accent of the first member. *bhare* — root *ḍubhṛñ bharaṇe*; Bhvādi; laṭ first person singular; since it follows a non-verb word, the *nighāta* accent.

*manīṣā* — *supāṃ sulug…* (Pā. 7-1-39) gives *luk* to the case-ending (*ṭā*). *kṣiyataḥ* — root *kṣi nivāsagatyoḥ*; Tudādi; śatṛ in the laṭ sense; *śa*-augment; *aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ…* (Pā. 6-4-77) gives *iyaṅ*; since the case-ending (*jas* or *ṅas*) follows a śatṛ without *num*, *śatur anumo nadyajādī* (Pā. 6-1-173) gives it the acute. *bhāvyasya* — the form is *bhāvayavyasya*; by Vedic usage a letter is lost. *amimīta* — root *māṅ māne*; Juhotyādi; laṅ third person singular *ta*; *juhotyādibhyaḥ śluḥ* (Pā. 2-4-75) gives *ślu* for the *śap*; *ślau* (Pā. 6-1-10) gives doubling of the root; *bhṛñāmit* (Pā. 7-4-76) gives *i* to the reduplicative syllable; *ī halyaghoḥ* (Pā. 6-4-113) gives *ī* for the final of the root, since it is *abhyasta*; the augment *aṭ*; since *yaḥ* is connected, no *nighāta*; since the augment is acute, first-syllable acute. *savān* — root *ṣuñ abhiṣave*; *dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ* gives *s*; *chandasi janasanakhanāṃ saṃ…* [print: "ಛಂದಸಿ ಜನಸನಖನಾಂ ಸಂ…" Pā. 3-2-67 [?]] gives *vanip*, … the suffix *ac* [print]; because of *cit*, *citaḥ* (Pā. 6-1-163) gives the final-acute; nominative plural. *atūrtaḥ* — root *turvī hiṃsāyām*; in the passive, the suffix *kta*; *rāllopaḥ* (Pā. 6-4-21) elides the *v* following the *r*; *hali ca* (Pā. 8-2-77) lengthens the penultimate; *na tūrtaḥ atūrtaḥ*; by *vyatyaya* the first-syllable acute of the latter member. *icchamānaḥ* — root *iṣu icchāyām*; by *vyatyaya* *śānac* in the laṭ sense, *śa*-augment; *iṣugamiyamāṃ chaḥ* (Pā. 7-3-77) gives *cha*; *āne muk* (Pā. 7-2-82) gives *muk*; since the *sārvadhātuka* follows the *upadeśa*, *tāsyanudāttet* (Pā. 6-1-186) makes it unaccented and the accent of the *śa* remains. ‖ 1 ‖

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> *śatam | rājñaḥ | nādhamānasya | niṣkān | śatam | aśvān | pra 'yatān | sadyaḥ | ādam |*
> *śatam | kakṣīvān | asurasya | gonām | divi | śravaḥ | ajaram | ā | tatāna ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> नाधमानस्य स्वीकर्तव्यमित्युच्चैर्याचमानस्यासुरस्य धनानां निरसितुर्दानशीलस्य राज्ञः स्वतेजसा दीप्यमानस्य सैनयस्य निष्कानाभरणविशेषान् इयत्ताविशेषविशिष्टानि वा सुवर्णानि शतसंख्याकानि । शतं सहस्रमित्यपरिमितवचनः । अपरिमितान् । सद्यः प्रार्थनानन्तरमेव कक्षीवानहमादम् । आत्तवानस्मि । स्वीकृतवानस्मीत्यर्थः । तथा प्रयतान् शुद्धान्लक्षणोपेतानाशुगमनसमर्थान्हयानश्वान्शतम् । आदम् । तथा गोनां पुंगवानां बलीवर्दानामित्यर्थः । उत्तरमन्त्रे स्त्रीगवीनामभिधानात् । तेषां शतमादम् । एवं प्रदाता राजा दिवि द्युलोके श्रवः कीर्तिमजरमजीर्णं शाश्वतीमा ततान । विस्तारितवान् । गवादिप्रतिग्रहीताहं स्वर्गे कीर्तिमकरवमित्यर्थः ॥

> *nādhamānasya svīkartavyamityuccairyācamānasyāsurasya dhanānāṃ nirasiturdānaśīlasya rājñaḥ svatejasā dīpyamānasya sainayasya niṣkānābharaṇaviśeṣān iyattāviśeṣaviśiṣṭāni vā suvarṇāni śatasaṃkhyākāni | śataṃ sahasramityaparimitavacanaḥ | aparimitān | sadyaḥ prārthanānantarameva kakṣīvānahamādam | āttavānasmi | svīkṛtavānasmītyarthaḥ | tathā prayatān śuddhānlakṣaṇopetānāśugamanasamarthānhayānaśvānśatam | ādam | tathā gonāṃ puṃgavānāṃ balīvardānāmityarthaḥ | uttaramantre strīgavīnāmabhidhānāt | teṣāṃ śatamādam | evaṃ pradātā rājā divi dyuloke śravaḥ kīrtimajaramajīrṇaṃ śāśvatīmā tatāna | vistāritavān | gavādipratigrahītāhaṃ svarge kīrtimakaravamityarthaḥ ‖*

*(Read from the image; a few words are small — "iyattāviśeṣa-viśiṣṭāni" and "balīvardānām" — and given as read.)* "Of the king who, begged with *nādhamānasya* — 'let it be accepted' — loudly urging, of the *asura* — the one who casts off riches, one who is given to giving, shining by his own splendour, Sainya — *niṣkān* — particular ornaments, or gold pieces of a definite number, a hundred in number. (*Śatam*, 'a hundred', is also a word for 'a thousand', not limiting: immeasurable.) *Sadyaḥ* — immediately after the asking — I, Kakṣīvat, *ādam* — took, accepted. Likewise *prayatān* — pure, with good marks, able to go swiftly, horses, *aśvān*, a hundred; I took. Likewise *gonām* — of bulls, oxen (since the next mantra speaks of cows); of them, a hundred I took. Thus the king who gave *divi* — in the heaven-world — *śravaḥ*, imperishable (*ajaram*), eternal fame, spread it out (*ā tatāna*): the sense is that I, the receiver of the gift of cows and the like, made his fame in heaven."

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *Kakṣīvān* — Kakṣīvat (I); *nādhamānasya* — [who] urgently begs, "let it be accepted"; *asurasya* — who gives wealth; *rājñaḥ* — (of the king called Svanaya); *śatam* — countless; *niṣkān* — *niṣkas*; *prayatān* — pure, of good marks; *śatam* — a hundred; *aśvān* — horses (and); *gonām* — of bulls; *śatam* — a hundred; *sadyaḥ* — at once (immediately after his asking); *ādam* — I took (the king, by giving); *divi* — in the world of heaven; *ajaram* — eternal; *śravaḥ* — (his) fame; *ā tatāna* — made to spread.

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** As soon as King Svanaya asked [me] to accept, I accepted the countless *niṣkas* he gave, a hundred pure horses, a hundred bulls; (having given gifts to me in this way) the king made his fame spread eternally in heaven (I, receiving the gifts, made his fame eternal in heaven).

### Printed p. 228  (PDF 249)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 18 Sū. 126".)*

**Printed English (as printed):** *From which generous prince, soliciting (my acceptance), I Kakshivat, unhesitatingly accepted a hundred nishkas, a hundred vigorous steeds, and a hundred bulls, whereby he has spread his imperishable fame through heaven.*

**Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 2.**

***nādhamānasya*** — for the word *nādhamānāḥ* the author of the Nirukta gives the meaning *yācamānāḥ*, "those who beg" (Ni. 4-3 [?], as printed). In the present ṛk, *svīkartavyam ity uccair yācamānasya* — "of the one who urgently begs 'it must be accepted'" — is an epithet of the word *rājñaḥ*, "of the king".

***asurasya*** — that many meanings are possible for the word *asura* has been shown in the special topics on Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-108-6 (Ṛk Saṃhitā, part 8, p. 59[?] — as printed "ಪೇ. ೫೯೭"? the numerals are unclear to me) and on ṛks 1-123-1 and 1-151-4. Among them there is the chief meaning "one who is given to giving". In the present ṛk, *dhanānāṃ nirasituḥ dānaśīlasya* — "one who casts off [gives] riches, given to giving" — it is an epithet of the word *rājñaḥ* (that is, of Svanaya).

***gonām*** — *puṃgavānāṃ balīvardānām ity arthaḥ*: "of bulls, of oxen".

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 2; noted briefly, numbers as read by the OCR).** *nādhamānasya* — root *nāthṛ yācñā…*; Bhvādi; *śānac* in the laṭ sense, *śap*; *āne muk* (Pā. 7-2-82) gives *muk*; since the *sārvadhātuka* follows the *upadeśa*, it is unaccented and the root-accent remains; genitive singular. *niṣkān* — root *ṣadḷ viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu*; *nau sader ḍiḥ* [print: "ನೌ ಸದೇರ್ಡಿಃ"] (Uṇ. 3-?) gives *ka* when *ni* is the upapada; by the marker *ḍ* the *ṭi* of the root is elided; final-acute by the suffix accent. *prayatān* — root *yam uparame*; *kta*; *anudāttopadeśavanatitanotyādīnām…* (Pā. 6-4-37) elides the nasal *m* of the root; *gatir anantaraḥ* (Pā. 6-2-49) gives the natural accent of the *gati* (*pra*); accusative plural. *ādam* — root *ḍudāñ dāne*; Juhotyādi; with *ā* as the upapada, *ādo 'nāsyavihasane* [print: "ಆಜೋ ದೋನಾಸ್ಯವಿಹರಣೇ" Pā. 1-3-20] would give *ātmanepada*, which does not occur here in the Veda; leṭ first person singular *mip*; *bahulaṃ chandasi* gives *luk* of the *śap*-substitute; *itaś ca lopaḥ parasmaipadeṣu* (Pā. 3-4-97) elides the *i* of the ending; *leṭo 'ṭāṭau* (Pā. 3-4-94) gives *aṭ* to it,

#### Ṛk 3

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> उप मा श्यावाः स्वनयेन दत्ता वधूमन्तो दश रथासो अस्थुः ।
> षष्टिः सहस्रमनु गव्यमागात्सनत्कक्षीवाँ अभिपित्वे अह्नाम् ॥ ३ ॥

> *upa mā śyāvāḥ svanayena dattā vadhūmanto daśa rathāso asthuḥ |*
> *ṣaṣṭiḥ sahasramanu gavyamāgātsanatkakṣīvā~ abhipitve ahnām ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> उप । मा । श्यावाः । स्वनयेन । दत्ताः । वधूऽमन्तः । दश । रथासः । अस्थुः ।
> षष्टिः । सहस्रम् । अनु । गव्यम् । आ । अगात् । सनत् । कक्षीवान् । अभिऽपित्वे । अह्नाम् ॥ ३ ॥

> *upa | mā | śyāvāḥ | svanayena | dattāḥ | vadhū 'mantaḥ | daśa | rathāsaḥ | asthuḥ |*
> *ṣaṣṭiḥ | sahasram | anu | gavyam | ā | agāt | sanat | kakṣīvān | abhi 'pitve | ahnām ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> स्वनयेन दत्ताः श्यावादर्वायुक्तत्वात् श्यावाः श्यावर्णाश्वयुक्ता वधूमन्तः आरूढाभिर्वधूभिस्तद्वन्तो दश दशसंख्याकाः रथासो रथा मा मामुपास्थुः । उपस्थिताः । गव्यशब्दो गोसमूहवाची । षष्टिः सहस्रमनु षष्ट्यधिकसहस्रं गवां समूहोऽन्वागात् । अनुगतः । ततः कक्षीवानात्मानं परोक्षेण ब्रवीति । तत्सर्वं प्रतिगृह्यायं

> कक्षीवानह्नां दिवसानां मध्येऽभिपित्वे सन्निहितेऽहनि सनत् । स्वीकृतं रथवाद्यादिकं स्वपित्रे समर्पयति स्वयं वा स्वीकरोति । अभिपित्वशब्द आसन्नकालवाची प्रपित्वशब्द इतिवत् । स च प्रपित्वेऽभीक इत्यासन्नस्येति यास्कोक्तत्वादासन्नवचनः । नि. ३-२० [?] । उपसर्गभेदेऽप्यर्थाभेदः ॥

> *kakṣīvānahnāṃ divasānāṃ madhye 'bhipitve sannihite 'hani sanat | svīkṛtaṃ rathavādyādikaṃ svapitre samarpayati svayaṃ vā svīkaroti | abhipitvaśabda āsannakālavācī prapitvaśabda itivat | sa ca prapitve 'bhīka ityāsannasyeti yāskoktatvādāsannavacanaḥ | ni. 3-20 [?] | upasargabhede 'pyarthābhedaḥ ‖*

*(Read from the image; the first clause continues the sentence begun at the foot of p. 229: "…having accepted all that, this Kakṣīvat …". The Nirukta number is printed "೩-೩೦" in the Special Topics and "೩-೨೦" in the bhāṣya; the OCR gives "३-२०" for the bhāṣya, "३-३०" for the topics — I leave both, doubtful.)* "…Kakṣīvat, in the day *abhipitve* — the near, present day, among the days (*ahnām*), *sanat* — [the one who] gives to his own father the chariots and the like accepted, or accepts them himself. The word *abhipitva* denotes near time, like the word *prapitva*; and that has the sense 'near', since Yāska says '*prapitve abhīke* means *āsannasya*' (Ni. 3-20 [?]): the sense is not different though the prefix differs."

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *Svanayena dattāḥ* — given by Svanaya; *śyāvāḥ* — dark-coloured (drawn by dark-coloured horses); *vadhūmantaḥ* — with my wives (accompanied by wives); *daśa* — ten; *rathāsaḥ* — chariots; *mā* — to me; *upa asthuḥ* — came near; *ṣaṣṭiḥ sahasram* — a thousand and sixty; *gavyam* — a herd of cows; *anu ā agāt* — followed; *kakṣīvān* — I, Kakṣīvat; *ahnām* — of the days; *abhipitve* — on the present (near) day; *sanat* — gave (to my father) (accepted).

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** King Svanaya gave me ten chariots drawn by dark horses and with my wives, and a thousand and sixty cows; (all of these) I offered (accepted) today [for you, that is, for the father].

**Printed English (as printed):** *Ten chariots drawn by bay steeds, and carrying my wives, stood near me, given me by Swanaya; and a thousand and sixty cows followed: these, after a short interval of time, did Kakshivat deliver (to his father).*

**Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 3.**

> अभिपित्वशब्दः आसन्नकालवाची प्रपित्वशब्द इतिवत् । स च प्रपित्वेऽभीक इत्यासन्नस्य ।

> *abhipitvaśabdaḥ āsannakālavācī prapitvaśabda itivat | sa ca prapitve 'bhīka ityāsannasya |*

(Ni. 3-30 [?], as printed.) *abhipitva* and *prapitva* — both words give the meaning "near, arrived". Since the author of the Nirukta has given for the word *prapitve* the meaning *abhīke* ("near"), and the word *abhipitve* has the same meaning, here *abhipitve* means "near". *Ahnām abhipitve* means "in the middle of many days" — the sense: "when the day arrives on which Kakṣīvat presented to his father the generous gifts given by Svanaya"; but, by the words *ahnām abhipitve*, the explanation "the end of the day, that is, in the evening he gave to his father" must not be taken; so some [scholars] explain…

### Printed p. 231  (PDF 252)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 11.)*

*(Special topics, Ṛk 3, continued from p. 230:)* …[some explain] that the gifts given by Svanaya in the morning, "*prātā ratnaṃ prātaritvā dadhāti*" (Ṛk 125-1), were offered [to the father] in the evening, and that this is in order; if one asks what the authority for this is, Sāyaṇa has given this meaning for the word *abhipitve*:

> आ वाजा यातोप न ऋभुक्षा महो नरो द्रविणसो गृणानाः ।
> आ वः पीतयोऽभिपित्वे अह्नामिमा अस्तं नवस्व इव ग्मन् ॥

> *ā vājā yātopa na ṛbhukṣā maho naro draviṇaso gṛṇānāḥ |*
> *ā vaḥ pītayo 'bhipitve ahnāmimā astaṃ navasva iva gman ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-34-5, as read from the print "೪-೩೪-೫".) *(Read letter by letter; "ā vājā yātopa na ṛbhukṣā" and the last pāda "astaṃ navasva iva gman" are as printed and in the OCR's garbled reading I cannot confirm them.)* In this ṛk he has explained *abhipitve* as *abhipatane samāpte* ("at the end of the day's coming-down") *tṛtīye savane* — "at the third pressing", that is, at the time of the third pressing, in the evening hour. Some hold that in the same way the present ṛk too may be so explained. The author of the Nirukta too, citing

> कुह स्विद्दोषा कुह वस्तोरश्विना कुहाभिपित्वं करतः कुहोषतुः ।
> को वां शयुत्रा विधवेव देवरं मर्यं न योषा कृणुते सधस्थ आ ॥

> *kuha sviddoṣā kuha vastoraśvinā kuhābhipitvaṃ karataḥ kuhoṣatuḥ |*
> *ko vāṃ śayutrā vidhaveva devaraṃ maryaṃ na yoṣā kṛṇute sadhastha ā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-40-2, as read from the print.) shows that there *abhipitvam* means *abhiprāptim* — "arriving, drawing near, coming" (Ni. 3-15 [?], as printed). Therefore the arrival may be the arrival in the morning, or the arrival in the evening.

There is still another doubt about this. About the words *abhipitva* and *prapitva* there is also discussion as to whether the root is *pat* or *āp*. Monier-Williams' Dictionary derives it from *abhi* + *pat*, giving one meaning "approaching" and another "close or departure of the day". According to the Nirukta the derivation must be *abhi* + *āp*; since Sāyaṇa gives meanings for this word in two ways, it seems that it may be formed from both roots *pat* and *āp*.

As Sāyaṇa says (1-126-3), some hold that identity of the two words *abhipitva* and *prapitva* cannot be maintained, and it is also the opinion of critics that they have not stated one fixed meaning for *abhipitva*. In this connection the criticism made by the scholar Bloomfield is worth noting. His examination runs thus:

> *The first explanation of* अभिपित्व *occurs at Nir. III. 15; it is* अभिप्राप्ति *'arrival', and so the word is explained by Sayana at R. V. I. 189-7;*

> **The first explanation of* abhipitva *occurs at Nir. III. 15; it is* abhiprāpti * 'arrival ', and so the word is explained by Sayana at R. V. I. 189-7;**

V. IV. 34-5 by 'Evening ' and in the same breath, as it were the word is rendered by 'forenoon '* divasasyābhipatane prātaḥkāle |*
> (*Journal of American Oriental Society, Vol. XVI. P. 25-26*).

*(Reproduced as printed, with the punctuation and spacing of the source; the Devanagari words within the English are printed in Devanagari in the source here.)* The summary of this opinion is that Sāyaṇa is somewhat confused in explaining the words *abhipitva* and *prapitva*. For example, in the ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-34-5 (cited above) he explains this word as "evening", and the same Sāyaṇa, in

> न संस्कृतं प्र मिमीतो गमिष्ठान्ति नूनमश्विनोपस्तुतेह ।
> दिवाभिपित्वेऽवसागमिष्ठा प्रत्यवर्तिं दाशुषे शम्भविष्ठा ॥

> *na saṃskṛtaṃ pra mimīto gamiṣṭhānti nūnamaśvinopastuteha |*
> *divābhipitve 'vasāgamiṣṭhā pratyavartiṃ dāśuṣe śambhaviṣṭhā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-76-3, as read from the print "೫-೭೬-೩".) — has explained the corresponding word as "forenoon" (*prātaḥkāla*): that is this critic's remark.

In the same way there are also the words *apapitva* and *sapitva*; with the word *pitva* are joined prefixes, and the formation of these four words and their meanings according to the contexts will be explained later.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 3; noted briefly, numbers as read by the OCR).** *dattāḥ* — root *ḍudāñ dāne*; *kta* in the passive; *do dad ghoḥ* (Pā. 7-4-46) gives *dad* for the root; *khari ca* gives the *car*; the form *dattāḥ*; nominative plural. *vadhūmantaḥ* — *vadhvaḥ yeṣāṃ santi iti vadhūmantaḥ*; *tad asyāsty asminn iti matup*; since *pit*, unaccented. *rathāsaḥ* — the word *ratha*; with *jas* following, *ājjaser asuk* (Pā. 7-1-50) gives *asuk*.

*(Read from the image; the OCR is badly garbled. The words marked [?] — "pajrādyannavantaḥ" and "cyāvayitrnnāḥ" — are small and doubtful in the print.)* "Of Dakṣaratha-… — *daśarathasya*: of him who has ten chariots, *sahasrasya* — of Kakṣīvat who is attended by a thousand followers, or [who has] a thousand herds of cows — *agre* — in front, *śoṇāḥ* — forty horses of red colour: since each chariot has four, the ten chariots together have forty horses; they too, taking a row (*śreṇi*), lead — bring the chariots to the desired place. Or else they make the chariots, yoked with horses, go in a line: four horses, in the form of a row, draw each chariot: that is the sense. Then those [horses], the *kakṣīvantaḥ* — those having *kakṣyā*, the girth-ropes (*kakṣyā* is a rope: 'kakṣyā rajjū rasvasya', says Yāska, Ni. 2-2) — or else all the sons of Aṅgiras are *kakṣīvantaḥ*; or, by the maxim of the servant, all of Kakṣīvat's followers are *kakṣīvantaḥ*; *pajrāḥ* — [fed with] food and the like — the *madacyutaḥ* — those that let their rut-fluid flow, high-spirited, the ones that make the pride of enemies fall; *kṛśanāvataḥ* — furnished with various golden ornaments (*kṛśana* is a name for gold: *kṛśanaṃ lohaṃ* are read among its names); the *atyān* — horses that go constantly — *ut amṛkṣanta* — they rub down excellently, to remove the sweat caused by the toil of the road."

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *Daśarathasya* — of him who is endowed with ten chariots; *sahasrasya* — of him who has a thousand followers (or: of him who has a thousand cows) (that is, of Kakṣīvat); *agre* — in front; *śoṇāḥ* — red; *catvāriṃśat* — forty (horses); *śreṇim* — in a row; *nayanti* — draw (the chariots); (*atha* — then); *kakṣīvantaḥ* — Kakṣīvat's followers; *pajrāḥ* — endowed with food; (*kakṣīvantaḥ* — those with girth-ropes); *madacyutaḥ* — [horses] dripping rut-fluid; *kṛśanāvataḥ* — endowed with golden ornaments; *atyān* — constantly moving (horses); *ut amṛkṣanta* — rub down well (limb by limb).

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** In front of Kakṣīvat, who has a thousand followers (and cows) and ten chariots, forty red horses draw the chariots in a row; then, provided with food such as grass, his followers rub down well the horses that are adorned with golden ornaments, constantly moving and dripping rut-fluid, tying them with ropes.

### Printed p. 235  (PDF 256)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 11.)*

**Printed English (as printed):** *Forty bay horses, (harnessed) to the chariots, lead the procession in front of a thousand (followers). The Pajras, the kinsmen of Kakshivat, rub down the high-spirited steeds, decorated with golden trappings.*

**Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 4.**

In this ṛk the number of horses and the number of chariots are stated, as it is described in

> शतमश्वाञ्छतं निष्कान्रथान्दश वधूमतः ।
> चतुर्युजो गवां चैव सहस्रं षष्ट्यधिकम् ॥

> *śatamaśvāñchataṃ niṣkānrathāndaśa vadhūmataḥ |*
> *caturyujo gavāṃ caiva sahasraṃ ṣaṣṭyadhikam ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 3-148 [?], as read.) — that ten chariots, a hundred horses and a thousand and sixty cows were displayed in front of Kakṣīvat.

***pajrāḥ*** — the meaning of this word is explained in the next ṛk.

***kakṣīvantaḥ*** — two kinds of meaning are stated for this word. First: *kakṣyā rajjū rasvasya* (Ni. 2-2): following the derivation of the author of the Nirukta, that the rope of a horse (the girth) has the name *kakṣyā*, the meaning is "followers of Kakṣīvat, who hold the horses". Second: because all the sons of the seer Aṅgiras are called by this name, it means "sons of Aṅgiras"; and it is for this reason that Dīrghatamas' son is also known by this name — [that is,] one possessed of the horse's rope, [that is,] one who is *aśvayuktaḥ*; and

> त्यं चिदश्वं न [?] वाजिनं [?] । [?] ।
> कक्षीवन्तं यदी पुना रथं न कृणुथो नवम् ॥

> *tyaṃ cidaśvaṃ na [?] vājinaṃ [?] | [?] |*
> *kakṣīvantaṃ yadī punā rathaṃ na kṛṇutho navam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-143-1, as read from the print; the first line is garbled in my reading and I do not complete it. *Kakṣīvantam yadī punā ratham na kṛṇutho navam* is clear.) — commenting on this ṛk Sāyaṇa states: here for the word *kakṣīvantam* he explains: *kakṣyā rajjū rasvasya tadvantam | dīrghatamasaḥ putraṃ uśijaḥ sutam ṛṣim* — "the one who has the rope of the horse: the son of Dīrghatamas, the seer, son of Uśij". In the present ṛk the meaning "followers of Kakṣīvat" is appropriate.

***kṛśanāvataḥ*** — the word *kṛśana* is recorded among the names of gold (Ni. 1-10 [?], as printed "೧-೧೦") and among the names of form (Ni. 3-13). Therefore it may be explained as "endowed with golden ornaments" or "possessing lovely forms". Yet its use in the sense "furnished with golden ornaments" is the more frequent.

***atyān*** — *satatagamanaśīlān aśvān* — "horses whose nature is constant going", ones that go without interruption.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 4; noted briefly, numbers as read by the OCR).** *daśarathasya* — *daśa rathāḥ yasya saḥ daśarathaḥ*; *bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam* (Pā. 6-2-1) gives the natural accent of the first member; genitive singular. *nayanti* — root *ṇīñ prāpaṇe*; laṭ third person plural; *tiṅ-nighāta*. *madacyutaḥ* — *madaṃ cyotayanti iti madacyutaḥ*; *kvip ca* (Pā. 3-2-76) gives *kvip*; *gatikārakopapadāt kṛt* gives the accent of the final member; accusative plural. *kṛśanāvataḥ* — *kṛśanāni hiraṇyāni yeṣāṃ santi iti kṛśanāvantaḥ*; *tad asyāsty asya* gives *matup*; *mādupadhāyāś ca…* gives *va* for *m*; since *pit* it is unaccented; *ā ṣa(?)… apidṛśyate* [print: "ಅನ್ಯೇಷಾಮಪಿ ದೃಶ್ಯತೇ" (Pā. 6-3-137)] gives lengthening in the Saṃhitā before the suffix; accusative plural. *kakṣīvantaḥ* — *kakṣe bhavā kakṣyā*: a rope belonging to the horse's belly; *bhave chandasi* (Pā. 4-4-110) gives *yat*; when the meaning "he has *kakṣyā*" is intended, *āsandīvad aṣṭhīvac cakrīvat kakṣīvad rumaṇvac ca* (Pā. 8-2-12) records *kakṣīvat* as formed, in the sense of a particular ṛṣi; the *ī* that is its substitute for the *yat*-suffix is given the acute by the *yat* suffix-accent; *matup* and *suṭ* [?] are unaccented because *pit*. *amṛkṣanta* — root *mṛjūś śuddhau*; since it shows a causative sense the root has included causative sense; *chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ* gives luṅ in the present sense; third person plural: *anta* substitution; *siC* for *cli*; *vraścabhrasja…* gives *ṣa* for the *j*; *ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si* gives *ka* for it; taking it as cause, *ṣatva* of the *s* of *siC*; the augment *aṭ*; *tiṅ-nighāta*. ‖ 4 ‖

> सुऽबन्धवः । ये । विश्याःऽइव । व्राः । अनस्वन्तः । श्रवः । ऐषन्त । पज्राः ॥ ५ ॥

> *pūrvām | anu | pra 'yatim | ā | dade | vaḥ | trīn | yuktān | aṣṭau | ari 'dhāyasaḥ | gāḥ |*
> *su 'bandhavaḥ | ye | viśyāḥ 'iva | vrāḥ | anasvantaḥ | śravaḥ | aiṣanta | pajrāḥ ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> इदानीमानीतं धनं बन्धुभ्यो निवेदयन्नाह । हे सुबन्धवः पूर्वां प्रयतिं पूर्वप्रदानमनु तमनुसृत्य वक्ष्यमाणानि रथादीनि वो युष्मदर्थमा ददे । स्वीकृतवानस्मि । यद्वा । पूर्वां प्रयतिं प्रदेयं रथादिकमनु दानक्रमेणैवा ददे । प्रतिगृहीतवानस्मि । कानि तानीति । त्रीनष्टौ च युक्तान् चतुर्भिश्चतुर्भिरश्वैर्धनैर्वा युक्तान् रथानिति शेषः । अत्र संख्यापृथग्निर्देशो न विवक्षितः । तथारिधायसो रिभिरीश्वरैर्धारणीया बहुमूल्या असंख्याता गाश्चादे । अत्र वक्ष्यमाणं पूर्वं प्रतिगृहीतावधिकानीति युक्तम् । पूर्वमेव पित्रे निवेदितानां पुनर्बन्धुभ्यो निवेदनासंभवात् । वधूमन्तो दश रथासो अस्थुरिति दशानां रथानामुक्तत्वादत्र त्रीनष्टौ चेत्येकादशानां वक्ष्यमाणत्वान्नवानां रथानामन्येभ्यो दातुमुचितत्वाच्चान्यानीति युक्तम् । उक्तानामेवानुवदनपक्षे दश वधूमन्तो रथा एको धनपूर्ण इति विवेकः । उक्तानामेव रथादीनां पुनर्विधानं प्रकृष्टत्वज्ञापनार्थं सर्वे ब्राह्मणा आगता वसिष्ठश्चागत इतिवत् । इदानीं परोक्षेणाह । सुबन्धवः शोभना विद्या योनिसंबन्धिनो येषां ते तथोक्ताः । यद्वा । शोभनबान्धवोपेताः परस्परमनुरागयुक्ता इत्यर्थः । विशः प्रजाः । तत्र भवा विश्याः । व्रियन्त इति वा व्रातः । तकारलोपश्छान्दसः । विशां व्राता यथा परस्परमनुरागवन्तस्तद्वत्सन्त इत्यर्थः । पज्रा अन्नवन्तोऽङ्गिरसः संतानप्रभवा ये सन्ति ते सर्वे सुबन्धवोऽनस्वन्तः शकटवन्तो हविर्धानशकटोपलक्षितसोमयागवन्तः सन्तः श्रवः सर्वत्र श्रूयमाणां कीर्तिमैषन्त । इच्छन्ति इच्छन्तु वा तदर्थमा ददे इति शेषः ॥

> *idānīmānītaṃ dhanaṃ bandhubhyo nivedayannāha | he subandhavaḥ pūrvāṃ prayatiṃ pūrvapradānamanu tamanusṛtya vakṣyamāṇāni rathādīni vo yuṣmadarthamā dade | svīkṛtavānasmi | yadvā | pūrvāṃ prayatiṃ pradeyaṃ rathādikamanu dānakrameṇaivā dade | pratigṛhītavānasmi | kāni tānīti | trīnaṣṭau ca yuktān caturbhiścaturbhiraśvairdhanairvā yuktān rathāniti śeṣaḥ | atra saṃkhyāpṛthagnirdeśo na vivakṣitaḥ | tathāridhāyaso ribhirīśvarairdhāraṇīyā bahumūlyā asaṃkhyātā gāścāde | atra vakṣyamāṇaṃ pūrvaṃ pratigṛhītāvadhikānīti yuktam | pūrvameva pitre niveditānāṃ punarbandhubhyo nivedanāsaṃbhavāt | vadhūmanto daśa rathāso asthuriti daśānāṃ rathānāmuktatvādatra trīnaṣṭau cetyekādaśānāṃ vakṣyamāṇatvānnavānāṃ rathānāmanyebhyo dātumucitatvāccānyānīti yuktam | uktānāmevānuvadanapakṣe daśa vadhūmanto rathā eko dhanapūrṇa iti vivekaḥ | uktānāmeva rathādīnāṃ punarvidhānaṃ prakṛṣṭatvajñāpanārthaṃ sarve brāhmaṇā āgatā vasiṣṭhaścāgata itivat | idānīṃ parokṣeṇāha | subandhavaḥ śobhanā vidyā yonisaṃbandhino yeṣāṃ te tathoktāḥ | yadvā | śobhanabāndhavopetāḥ parasparamanurāgayuktā ityarthaḥ | viśaḥ prajāḥ | tatra bhavā viśyāḥ | vriyanta iti vā vrātaḥ | takāralopaśchāndasaḥ | viśāṃ vrātā yathā parasparamanurāgavantastadvatsanta ityarthaḥ | pajrā annavanto 'ṅgirasaḥ saṃtānaprabhavā ye santi te sarve subandhavo 'nasvantaḥ śakaṭavanto havirdhānaśakaṭopalakṣitasomayāgavantaḥ santaḥ śravaḥ sarvatra śrūyamāṇāṃ kīrtimaiṣanta | icchanti icchantu vā tadarthamā dade iti śeṣaḥ ‖*

*(Read from the image; the OCR confirms the structure but is garbled in the middle. The bhāṣya of this ṛk is long, in small type; I give it as read, with the doubtful clause "ayam eva yuktam / vadhūmanto … anyānīti" as printed — "[?]" marks are not needed where the print was clear to me, but the middle (from "atra vakṣyamāṇaṃ" to "anyānīti yuktam") is only partly legible and may contain slips.)* "Now, announcing to his kinsmen the wealth brought: O *subandhavaḥ* — O good kinsmen — *pūrvām prayatim anu* — following the earlier gift — the chariots and the rest that are going to be named, *vaḥ* — for you — *ā dade*: I have accepted. Or else: following the gift to be given — the chariots and the rest — in the order of giving, I have taken it, accepted. What are they? *Trīn aṣṭau ca yuktān* — eleven chariots yoked with four horses each or with wealth. Here the separate statement of the number is not intended. Likewise, *aridhāyasaḥ* — to be held by *ari*, by lords: valuable, countless — and cows I took. … [The text then argues that these eleven chariots are in addition to the ten already mentioned, since what was presented earlier to the father cannot be presented again to the kinsmen; 'ten chariots with wives' were stated, here 'three and eight', eleven, are to be stated; so the others are for giving to others.] If the sense is only a repetition of what was said, then there are ten chariots with wives, and one full of wealth: that is the distinction. The re-statement of the chariots already stated is to show their excellence, as in 'all the Brahmins have come, and Vasiṣṭha has come'. Now he speaks indirectly: *subandhavaḥ* — those whose kinship by birth (or by knowledge) is good; or those having good kinsmen, that is, bound by mutual affection. *Viśaḥ* are subjects; those who belong to them are *viśyāḥ*. *Vrāḥ* is *vrātāḥ* (or: those that are chosen); the loss of *t* is Vedic. As troops of subjects are attached to each other, so [you] are: that is the sense. *Pajrāḥ* — those Aṅgirases, endowed with food, who are the offspring [of the line], all *subandhavaḥ*, *anasvantaḥ* — possessing carts, performing the Soma sacrifice, marked by the carts for the *havirdhāna* — may they desire (*aiṣanta*) *śravaḥ* — fame heard of everywhere; for that [purpose] I have accepted it: this is the remainder."

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *He subandhavaḥ* — O good kinsmen; *pūrvām* — said before; *prayatim anu* — following the gift (following the order of gifts); *trīn aṣṭau [ca]* — eleven; *yuktān* — yoked (with horses or with wealth) (chariots); *aridhāyasaḥ* — fit to be held by lords (countless and priceless); *gāḥ ca* — and cows; *vaḥ* — for you; *ā dade* — I have accepted; *ye pajrāḥ* — those Aṅgirases (endowed with food); *subandhavaḥ* — those of good kinship; *vrāḥ* — (those of one troop), like *viśyāḥ iva* — like subjects (full of mutual love); *(subandhavaḥ — those my kinsmen all)*; *anasvantaḥ* — possessing carts (suited to the Soma sacrifice, those having carts to carry green food); *śravaḥ* — fame (heard of everywhere); *aiṣanta* — desire (let them desire).

### Printed p. 238  (PDF 259)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 18 Sū. 126".)*

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** O kinsmen, for you I have accepted cows fit for kings, eleven chariots endowed with wealth, of the kind of the gift mentioned before; (accepting these things) may all my kinsmen, bound together in mutual love, perform Soma sacrifices and gain fame.

**Printed English (as printed):** *I have accepted a prior grant, (kinsmen), for you : three and eight harnessed chariots and cattle of incalculable value : may the kindred Pajras, like well-disposed relations, be desirous of acqiring renown by their abundant offerings.* *(sic: "acqiring")*

**Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 5.**

***aridhāyasaḥ*** — *aribhir īśvarair dharaṇīyāḥ bahumūlyā asaṃkhyātāḥ*: "to be held by lords (*īśvara*), that is, by wealthy persons; of great price; countless" — an epithet of cows. How the sense "lord" came to the word *ari* is explained by the author of the Nirukta thus: *arir amitram ṛcchateḥ | īśvaro 'ris tasmād eva* (Ni. 5-7 [?], as printed "೫-೭"): from the root *ṛ* meaning "to hurt", the word *ari* with the sense "enemy", as also, for the lord who has authority over servants, the name *ari* — and citing

> पुरु त्वा दाश्वान्वोचेऽरिरग्ने तव स्विदा । तोदस्येव शरण आ महस्य ॥

> *puru tvā dāśvānvoce 'riragne tava svidā | todasyeva śaraṇa ā mahasya ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-150-1, as printed "೧-೧೫೦-೧"; *"tvā dāśvān"* as read.) as he says that the word *ari* means "lord", so in the present sūkta also the same meaning arises. That is: "a rich man fit to possess priceless cows".

### Printed p. 239  (PDF 260)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 11.)*

***pajrāḥ*** — the word *pajra* gives the same meaning in the previous ṛk and in this ṛk. Though here *pajrāḥ* is meant for Aṅgirases, the word is used in the sense of "those who have abundant food". In the previous ṛk Sāyaṇa explained it as *ghāsādyannavantaḥ santaḥ* — "being provided with food such as grass"; in the same way, in this sūkta too, *annavanto 'ṅgirasaḥ* — "Aṅgirases who have abundant food". The author of the Nirukta, citing

> य इन्द्राग्नी सुतेषु वां स्तवत्तेष्वृतावृधा । जोषवाकं वदतः पज्रहोषिणा न देवा भसथश्चन ॥

> *ya indrāgnī suteṣu vāṃ stavatteṣvṛtāvṛdhā | joṣavākaṃ vadataḥ pajrahoṣiṇā na devā bhasathaścana ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-59-4, as read from the print "೬-೫೯-೪".) explains there *pajrahoṣiṇā* as *prārjitahoṣiṇaḥ*; of this Durgācārya says *prabhūtayāgau* — "[the two] of abundant sacrifice". By *pajra* the lineage of the Aṅgirases is also meant; the purport is "those who have abundant wealth". The *pajra* lineage is a famous name in the Ṛk Saṃhitā.

> एतानि वां श्रवस्या सुदानू ब्रह्माङ्गूषं सदनं रोदस्योः ।
> यद्वां पज्रासो अश्विना हवन्ते यातमिषा च विदुषे च वाजम् ॥

> *etāni vāṃ śravasyā sudānū brahmāṅgūṣaṃ sadanaṃ rodasyoḥ |*
> *yadvāṃ pajrāso aśvinā havante yātamiṣā ca viduṣe ca vājam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-112-10, as read from the print.) — in these and other ṛks the name of the *pajra* lineage is praised. Since Kakṣīvat was born in this lineage, he too has the name *pajriya*.

> प्र या घोषे भृगवाणे न शोभे ययां वाचा यजति पज्रियो वाम् ।
> प्रैषयुर्न विद्वान् ॥

> *pra yā ghoṣe bhṛgavāṇe na śobhe yayāṃ vācā yajati pajriyo vām |*
> *praiṣayurna vidvān ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-120-5, as read from the print.) — in this ṛk *pajriyaḥ* is explained: *pajrā āṅgirasaḥ teṣāṃ kulotpannaḥ kakṣīvān* — "Kakṣīvat born in the family of the Pajras, the Aṅgirases".

> सुषुप्सा वां वरुण मित्र रातिर्गवां शता पृक्षयामेषु पज्रे ।
> श्रुतरथे प्रियरथे दधानाः सद्यः पुष्टिं निरुन्धानासो अग्मन् ॥

> *suṣupsā vāṃ varuṇa mitra rātirgavāṃ śatā pṛkṣayāmeṣu pajre |*
> *śrutarathe priyarathe dadhānāḥ sadyaḥ puṣṭiṃ nirundhānāso agman ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-122-7 [?], as read from the print; "suṣupsā" is as read and doubtful.) — here too Kakṣīvat says of himself that he belongs to the Pajra lineage and that he is able in the management of sacrifices with abundant gifts of food. In the same way, in the present ṛk Sāyaṇa has explained *pajrā* as *annavantaḥ aṅgirasaḥ*.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 5; noted briefly, numbers as read by the OCR and the page).** *prayatim* — root *yam uparame*; *ktin*; *anudāttopadeśa…* (Pā. 6-4-37) elides the nasal *m* of the root; in the *prādi*-compound, *tādau ca niti kṛty atiḥ* (Pā. 6-2-50) as an exception to the accent of the final member gives the natural accent of the *gati* (*pra*); accusative singular. *dade* — root *ḍudāñ dāne*; liṭ first person singular; since it follows a non-verb word, the *nighāta*. *yuktān* — root *yujir yoge*; *niṣṭhā* gives *kta*; *coḥ kuḥ* gives *ku* for the *j*; final-acute by the suffix; accusative plural. *aridhāyasaḥ* — *aribhiḥ dharaṇīyāḥ aridhāyasaḥ tān*; root *ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*; *vahihāhādhāñbhyaś chandasi* (Uṇ. 4-?) gives *asun*; the preceding sūtra's *ṇit* is carried on, so *āto yuk ciṇkṛtoḥ* (Pā. 7-3-33) gives the augment *yuk*; the form *dhāyas*. *subandhavaḥ* — *śobhanāḥ bandhavaḥ yeṣāṃ te subandhavaḥ*; *nañsubhyām* would give the final-acute, but as an exception *bahuvrīhau ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasi* (Pā. 6-2-119) gives the first-syllable acute of the latter member; nominative plural. *viśyāḥ* — *viśi bhavāḥ viśyāḥ*; *yat* in the sense of "belonging to"; *tit svaritam* (Pā. 6-1-185) gives the *svarita*. *vrāḥ* — *vriyante iti vrāḥ*; the form *vrātāḥ*; the loss of *t* is Vedic; or else *ghaṅarthe kavidhānam* gives the suffix *ka*. *anasvantaḥ* — *anaḥ* means a cart; *anāṃsi yeṣāṃ santi iti anasvantaḥ*; since *ap* [as printed] follows, *mādupadhāyāś ca…* gives *va* for the *m* of *matup*; since *pit*, unaccented. *aiṣanta* — root *iṣu icchāyām*; *chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ* (Pā. 3-4-6) gives laṅ in the present sense; by *vyatyaya*, *ātmanepada*; likewise *iṣugamiyamāṃ chaḥ* does not give the *cha*, in the Veda; in the third person plural

#### Ṛk 6

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> आगधिता परिगधिता या कशीकेव जङ्गहे ।
> ददाति मह्यं यादुरी याशूनां भोज्या शता ॥ ६ ॥

> *āgadhitā parigadhitā yā kaśīkeva jaṅgahe |*
> *dadāti mahyaṃ yādurī yāśūnāṃ bhojyā śatā ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> आऽगधिता । परिऽगधिता । या । कशीकाऽइव । जङ्गहे ।
> ददाति । मह्यम् । यादुरी । याशूनाम् । भोज्या । शता ॥ ६ ॥

> *ā 'gadhitā | pari 'gadhitā | yā | kaśīkā 'iva | jaṅgahe |*
> *dadāti | mahyam | yādurī | yāśūnām | bhojyā | śatā ‖ 6 ‖*

*(The word "yāśūnām" is as printed in the Saṃhitā and Pada; the bhāṣya below explains it with "yaśa".)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> संभोगाय प्रार्थितो भावयव्यः स्वभार्यां रोमशामप्रौढेति बुद्ध्वा परिहसन्नाह । भोज्या भोगयोग्याग्धिता [?] आ समन्ताद्गृहीता स्वीकृता । तथा परिगधिता परितो गृहीता । आदरातिशयाय पुनर्वचनम् । गध्यं गृह्णातेरिति यास्कः । नि. ५-१५ । यद्वा । आगधिता आसमन्तादाश्रयन्ती । अन्तरं प्रजननेन वाक्यं भुजादिभिरित्यर्थः [?] । गद्यतिर्मिथोभावकर्मेति यास्कः । नि. ५-१५ । पूर्वस्मिन्पक्षे पुरुषस्य प्राधान्यमुत्तरस्मिन्स्त्रिया योषिता इति भेदः । कीदृशी सा । या जङ्गहे अत्यर्थं गृह्णाति कदाचिदपि न मुञ्चति । अत्याग्रे दृष्टान्तः । कशीकेव । कशीका नाम सुतवत्सा नकुली । सा यथा पत्या सह चिरकालं क्रीडति न कदाचिदपि विमुञ्चति तद्वदेषापि । किंच भोज्यैषा यादुरी । यादुरिर्यादनाम् [?] रेतोलक्षणमुदकं प्रभूतं ददातीति यादुरी । बहुरेतोयुक्तेत्यर्थः । तादृशी सती याशूनां संभोगानां । यश इति प्रजननं नाम तत्संबन्धीनि कर्माणि यशूनि भोगाः तेषां शता शतान्यसंख्यातानि मह्यं ददाति ॥

> *saṃbhogāya prārthito bhāvayavyaḥ svabhāryāṃ romaśāmaprauḍheti buddhvā parihasannāha | bhojyā bhogayogyāgdhitā [?] ā samantādgṛhītā svīkṛtā | tathā parigadhitā parito gṛhītā | ādarātiśayāya punarvacanam | gadhyaṃ gṛhṇāteriti yāskaḥ | ni. 5-15 | yadvā | āgadhitā āsamantādāśrayantī | antaraṃ prajananena vākyaṃ bhujādibhirityarthaḥ [?] | gadyatirmithobhāvakarmeti yāskaḥ | ni. 5-15 | pūrvasminpakṣe puruṣasya prādhānyamuttarasminstriyā yoṣitā iti bhedaḥ | kīdṛśī sā | yā jaṅgahe atyarthaṃ gṛhṇāti kadācidapi na muñcati | atyāgre dṛṣṭāntaḥ | kaśīkeva | kaśīkā nāma sutavatsā nakulī | sā yathā patyā saha cirakālaṃ krīḍati na kadācidapi vimuñcati tadvadeṣāpi | kiṃca bhojyaiṣā yādurī | yāduriryādanām [?] retolakṣaṇamudakaṃ prabhūtaṃ dadātīti yādurī | bahuretoyuktetyarthaḥ | tādṛśī satī yāśūnāṃ saṃbhogānāṃ | yaśa iti prajananaṃ nāma tatsaṃbandhīni karmāṇi yaśūni bhogāḥ teṣāṃ śatā śatānyasaṃkhyātāni mahyaṃ dadāti ‖*

*(Read from the image; the OCR is partly garbled. The words "agdhitā [?]" in the first sentence — the print has "bhojyā bhogayogyāgdhitā", which I read as "…āgadhitā" — and "yādanāma [?]" are doubtful.)* "Having been asked for union, Bhāvayavya, realising that his own wife Romaśā is not mature, says it, laughing. *Bhojyā* — fit for enjoyment, *āgadhitā* — taken on all sides, accepted; likewise *parigadhitā* — taken all round; the repetition is for the sake of great regard: '*gadhyaṃ gṛhṇāteḥ*', says Yāska (Ni. 5-15). Or else *āgadhitā* — one who approaches from all sides … with the inner [that is, secret] speech by procreation, by arms and the rest: '*gadyatir mitho-bhāvakarmā*', says Yāska (Ni. 5-15). In the first view the man is the principal one; in the latter, the woman: that is the difference. What is she like? She who *jaṅgahe* — grips exceedingly, never lets go. A simile of the strong grasp: *kaśīkā iva* — *kaśīkā* is the weasel with young; as she plays long with her mate and never lets him go, so she. Moreover this enjoyable one is *yādurī*: *yādurī* — she who gives much water in the form of semen, i.e. rich in semen. Such a one *yāśūnām* — of acts of union: *yaśa* is a name for procreation; the acts connected with it, *yaśūni*, are enjoyments; hundreds, countless, of these she gives to me."

### Printed p. 242  (PDF 263)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 18 Sū. 126".)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *Bhojyā* — fit for enjoyment; *yā* — which (Romaśā); *āgadhitā* — accepted (and); *parigadhitā* — embraced; *kaśīkā iva* — like a female weasel; *jaṅgahe* — [she] who tightly clasps; (*sā* — she); *yādurī* — one richly provided with the water of semen; *yāśūnām śatā* — hundreds (countless) of acts of enjoyment; *mahyam* — to me; *dadāti* — gives.

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** Romaśā, fit for enjoyment, accepted, clasps tightly like a female weasel; and, being rich in semen, gives me endless pleasures of union.

**Printed English (as printed):** *She, who, when her desires are assented to, clings as tenaciously as a female weasel, and who is ripe for enjoyment, yields me infinite delight.*

**Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 6.**

This ṛk and the next are the conversation between Bhāvayavya and his wife Romaśā. This Romaśā is the daughter of Bṛhaspati; at one time, with a desire for union, she went to her husband Bhāvayavya and asked that her desire be satisfied; in reply to that, Bhāvayavya spoke this ṛk. In reply to Bhāvayavya's words, Romaśā speaks the next ṛk. In these two ṛks, as in a dialogue of union, there is no matter such as the praise of a deity, which is common to sūktas and ṛks. Since the talk of union in these ṛks is not connected with the subject of this sūkta, some express doubt as to how it came to be included here. Moreover, of the seven ṛks of this sūkta, the first five are of Triṣṭubh metre and only these two ṛks are of Anuṣṭubh metre; so they are not a part of this sūkta. Somehow, for some other reason, they have been included here. It is indeed a wonder that matters of private life, unconnected with the subject, have been inserted into ṛks and included here.

The main idea of this ṛk and of the next may be stated thus: Bhāvayavya and his wife Romaśā speak teasingly to each other; Bhāvayavya, speaking indirectly, says in this way —

---

### Printed p. 243  (PDF 264)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 11.)*

*(Special topics, Ṛk 6, continued — the dialogue:)* **Bhāvayavya** (teasing his wife Romaśā): "O, this Romaśā, like a female weasel that never lets go of her beloved male weasel, once she has clasped him (for enjoyment), wishes to embrace me a hundred times. Her body is full (or: wet) with semen."

**Romaśā:** "O husband, do not laugh at me as being young in age and not fit for union. Come to my side (for union), and embrace me well, clasping my limbs. Do not suppose that my limbs are not yet well grown and thus not fit for union. For my womb and other parts are thickly covered with well-grown hair, like the body of a ewe of the Gandhāra country."

The main subject here is this: when Romaśā, with desire, begged her husband, Bhāvayavya laughed at his wife as being young in age and not fit for union. In answer to that, Romaśā says that she is not a girl but a grown woman fit for union, and, to make this firm, gives an example. In the state of manhood, the hair on the hands and feet and the other limbs is naturally thick, and it indicates that they have passed boyhood and have come into youth; but for women, when they are in youth, hair on hands and feet is unusual — one may say impossible; but on the head, and chiefly in the region of the womb, thickly grown hair indicates the state of youth. Therefore, to support the point that she is in youth and fit for union, Romaśā tells the example that her womb region, like a ewe of the Gandhāra country or like the womb of a pregnant woman, is full of hair. The country of Gandhāra must be the country near Kandahar (the print has "Kandahar" in Latin letters); since that is a cold country, the sheep and other animals have much hair; so that example is told here.

***āgadhitā, parigadhitā*** — in giving the derivation of these words, Yāska takes this very ṛk as the example, saying:

> गध्यतिर्भावकर्मा । आगधिता परिगधिता इत्यपि निगमो भवति ।

> *gadhyatirbhāvakarmā | āgadhitā parigadhitā ityapi nigamo bhavati |*

(Ni. 5-15 [?], as printed "೫-೧೫".) The word *gadhyati* means "mixing, uniting". Therefore in the present ṛk the "mixing of the limbs of husband and wife" means that the limbs of both are in contact with each other, one embracing the other;

### Printed p. 244  (PDF 265)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 18 Sū. 126".)*

this is the idea that the bhāṣyakāra indicates. Therefore the idea is that the two words *āgadhitā* and *parigadhitā* have the same sense, with a slight difference of more or less. In this matter Durgācārya, the commentator on the Nirukta, has given this explanation for the ṛk:

> आगधितेति भावयव्यस्यार्षम् । आगधिता आगृहीता अभिमिश्रिता च । परिगधिता च परिमिश्रिता बाहुभ्यां मया परिष्वक्तेत्यर्थः । या कशीकेव प्रतिकशं कशीकेव स हि नकुलजातिः काञ्चिद्दीने कशामिति श्रूयतेऽश्वमेधे । सा यथा मदकाले प्रतिकशमतितरां परिष्वजति स हि तस्याः परिष्वजनस्वभावः । एवं या मा आजंगहे परिगृह्णाति बाहुभ्याम् । परिगृह्य च ददाति । यादुरीया आदरवती । अथवा यादः रेतःसेकेन तदस्यास्तीति । यादः इत्युदकनामसु पठितम् । आह किं ददाति मह्यम् ? इति । उच्यते — याशूनां मैथुनाख्यानां शता शतानि बहुश इत्यर्थः । या एवंप्रकारा सा मम भोज्या पत्नीत्यभिप्रायः । एवमत्र मैथुनसंबन्धात्शब्दसारूप्याच्च गध्यतिर्मिश्रीभावकर्मेत्युपपद्यते ॥

> *āgadhiteti bhāvayavyasyārṣam | āgadhitā āgṛhītā abhimiśritā ca | parigadhitā ca parimiśritā bāhubhyāṃ mayā pariṣvaktetyarthaḥ | yā kaśīkeva pratikaśaṃ kaśīkeva sa hi nakulajātiḥ kāñciddīne kaśāmiti śrūyate 'śvamedhe | sā yathā madakāle pratikaśamatitarāṃ pariṣvajati sa hi tasyāḥ pariṣvajanasvabhāvaḥ | evaṃ yā mā ājaṃgahe parigṛhṇāti bāhubhyām | parigṛhya ca dadāti | yādurīyā ādaravatī | athavā yādaḥ retaḥsekena tadasyāstīti | yādaḥ ityudakanāmasu paṭhitam | āha kiṃ dadāti mahyam ? iti | ucyate — yāśūnāṃ maithunākhyānāṃ śatā śatāni bahuśa ityarthaḥ | yā evaṃprakārā sā mama bhojyā patnītyabhiprāyaḥ | evamatra maithunasaṃbandhātśabdasārūpyācca gadhyatirmiśrībhāvakarmetyupapadyate ‖*

(Ni. 5-15 [?]; as printed "೩-೧೫"; the OCR reads "३-१५".) *(Read letter by letter; the Sanskrit of this long Durga passage is partly in small type, and the words I am least sure of are "kāñcid dīne kaśām" and "svabhāvaḥ"; I mark them as read, without completing.)* "'*Āgadhitā*' is a word of Bhāvayavya's [verse]. *Āgadhitā* — accepted, mixed, *parigadhitā* — mixed all round, embraced by me with the arms: this is the sense. *Kaśīkā iva* — the *kaśīkā*, namely a weasel-kind; … as she at the time of rut embraces him closely [the male], for embracing is her nature; so she who, taking hold of me, grips with the arms, and having gripped, gives. *Yādurī* — [one] with abundance; or, from *yādaḥ*, water, [she] has it by the sprinkling of semen (*yādaḥ* is read among the names of water). What does she give me? It is said: of *yāśūnām* — [acts] called union — hundreds, many times: that is the sense. Such a one is my enjoyable wife: this is the intention. Thus here, by the connection with union and by similarity of the word, '*gadhyatir miśrībhāvakarma*' (*gadhyati* means the act of mixing) is established."

The chief meaning of this we have already explained, so there is no need to repeat it.

***kaśīkā*** — *kaśīkā nāma sūtavatsā nakulī*: a female weasel who has just given birth. Sāyaṇa explains the fitness of the simile thus: *sā yathā patyā saha cirakālaṃ krīḍati na kadācid api vimuñcati tadvadeṣāpi* — after giving birth, the female weasel, wishing union with her mate, does not leave him, and remains with him, fully satisfying the mate's desire. Here Bhāvayavya's wife Romaśā, like the female weasel, does not leave the husband but embraces him; so the example is given. And "*jaṅgahe*", the verb, is a repetition (a form of intensity) and denotes the nature of the embrace.

***yādurī*** — the word *yādurī* (*yādus*) is recorded among the names of water; here it means "water in the form of semen".

***yāśūnām*** — *yaśa iti prajananānāma | tatsaṃbandhīni karmāṇi yāśūni bhogāḥ*: *yaśa* is a name of procreation; the acts connected with it are *yāśūni*, "enjoyments": the meaning is "pleasures of union and the like that are the means of begetting offspring".

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 6; noted briefly, numbers as read by the OCR).** *āgadhitā* — the root *gadh* is used in the sense of "taking". '*gadhyaṃ gṛhṇāteḥ*' (Ni. 5-15), says Yāska. In the passive, the suffix *kta*; the augment *iṭ*; *gatir anantaraḥ* (Pā. 6-2-49)

### Printed p. 245  (PDF 266)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 11.)*

gives the natural accent of the *gati* (*ā*); the same process in *parigadhitā*; in the feminine *ṭāp*, since it ends in *a*. *jaṅgahe* — root *grah upādāne*; when intensity is shown, *dhātor ekāco halādeḥ kriyāsamabhihāre yaṅ* (Pā. 3-1-22) gives *yaṅ*; *yaṅo ci ca* (Pā. 2-4-74) gives *luk* of it, by the *caṅ*-mitta; by *vyatyayo bahulam* the *ātmanepada*; in the Veda the reduplicative syllable gets *nuk* and the *r* is elided; after the *yaṅluk*-ending, third person singular; since *yat* is connected [with it], no *nighāta*; *abhyastānām ādiḥ* (Pā. 6-1-189) gives the first-syllable acute. *dadāti* — root *ḍudāñ dāne*; Juhotyādi; laṭ third person singular; since it stands at the head of a pāda, no *nighāta*; the first-syllable acute as before. *yādurī* — root *dā dāne*; *yādum dadāti iti*; *ātoʼnupasarge kaḥ* (Pā. 3-2-3) gives the suffix *ka*; in the feminine, by Vedic usage, *ī*; the words *yādurī* and *yāśū* are established by *pṛṣodarādīni yathopadiṣṭam* (Pā. 6-3-109). *bhojyā* — *bhoktuṃ yogyā bhojyā*; root *bhuja pālanābhyavahārayoḥ*; *ṛhaloṇyat* (Pā. 3-1-124) gives *ṇyat*; *pugantalaghūpadhasya ca* gives guṇa of the short penultimate; by *vyatyaya* no *kutva*; *tit svaritam* (Pā. 6-1-185) gives the *svarita*; in the feminine *ṭāp*. *śatā* — *śeś chandasi bahulam* (Pā. 6-1-70) gives the elision of *śi* in the neuter form. ‖ 6 ‖

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> उपऽउप । मे । परा । मृश । मा । मे । दभ्राणि । मन्यथाः ।

> *sarvā | aham | asmi | romaśā | gandhārīṇām 'iva | avikā ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> रोमशा नाम बृहस्पतेः पुत्री ब्रह्मवादिनी परिहसन्तं स्वपतिं प्रत्याह । भो पते मे माम् । द्वितीयार्थे चतुर्थी । उपोप । द्वितीय उपशब्दः पादपूरणः । उपेत्य परा मृश । सम्यक् स्पृश । भोगयोग्यामवगत्येत्यर्थः । यद्वा । मे मम गोपनीयमङ्गं मुपोप परामृश । अत्यन्तं नान्तरं स्वकीयं परामर्शभावशङ्कां निवारयति । मे मदङ्गानि रोमाणि दभ्राणि मा मन्यथाः । अल्पानि मा बुद्ध्यस्व । दभ्रमर्भकमित्यल्पस्येति दभ्रं दभ्नोतेरिति यास्कः । नि. ३-२० । अदभ्रत्वमेव विशदयति । अहं रोमशा बहुरोमयुक्तास्मि । यतोऽहमीदृश्यतः सर्वा संपूर्णावयवास्मि । रोमशत्वे दृष्टान्तः । गन्धारीणामविकेव । गन्धारा केशां संबन्धिन्यो विजातिरिव [?] । तद्देशस्था आनवो मेषा यथा रोमशाः कथाहमस्मि । देशः । यद्वा । गन्धारीणां गर्भधारिणीनां स्त्रीणामविकार्थं तर्पयन्ती योनिरिव । तासामा प्रसवं रोमादिविकर्तनस्य शास्त्रे निषिद्धत्वाद्योनिः रोमशा भवति । अतः सोपमियते । यतोऽयं सर्वादृशीतो मामुपैहीं माम् [?] । मावबुध्यस्वेत्यर्थः ॥

> *romaśā nāma bṛhaspateḥ putrī brahmavādinī parihasantaṃ svapatiṃ pratyāha | bho pate me mām | dvitīyārthe caturthī | upopa | dvitīya upaśabdaḥ pādapūraṇaḥ | upetya parā mṛśa | samyak spṛśa | bhogayogyāmavagatyetyarthaḥ | yadvā | me mama gopanīyamaṅgaṃ mupopa parāmṛśa | atyantaṃ nāntaraṃ svakīyaṃ parāmarśabhāvaśaṅkāṃ nivārayati | me madaṅgāni romāṇi dabhrāṇi mā manyathāḥ | alpāni mā buddhyasva | dabhramarbhakamityalpasyeti dabhraṃ dabhnoteriti yāskaḥ | ni. 3-20 | adabhratvameva viśadayati | ahaṃ romaśā bahuromayuktāsmi | yato 'hamīdṛśyataḥ sarvā saṃpūrṇāvayavāsmi | romaśatve dṛṣṭāntaḥ | gandhārīṇāmavikeva | gandhārā keśāṃ saṃbandhinyo vijātiriva [?] | taddeśasthā ānavo meṣā yathā romaśāḥ kathāhamasmi | deśaḥ | yadvā | gandhārīṇāṃ garbhadhāriṇīnāṃ strīṇāmavikārthaṃ tarpayantī yoniriva | tāsāmā prasavaṃ romādivikartanasya śāstre niṣiddhatvādyoniḥ romaśā bhavati | ataḥ sopamiyate | yato 'yaṃ sarvādṛśīto māmupaihīṃ mām [?] | māvabudhyasvetyarthaḥ ‖*

*(Read from the image; the middle of this bhāṣya — from "nāntaraṃ svakīyaṃ" to "mām" — is small and I have transcribed only what is legible; the words marked [?] are doubtful and the OCR here is badly garbled. The sense is secure from the Kannada pratipadārtha and the p. 247 comment.)* "Romaśā, the daughter of Bṛhaspati, a *brahmavādinī*, says to her husband who is teasing: O husband, *me* — to me (the dative has the sense of the accusative); *upopa* — the second *upa* is a pāda-filler; coming near, *parā mṛśa* — touch properly, understanding that I am fit for enjoyment. Or else: touch my part that is to be hidden; she dispels the doubt about the touch. *Me dabhrāṇi mā manyathāḥ* — do not think my limbs, my hairs, *dabhrāṇi* — small, few: '*dabhram arbhakam alpasya*', '*dabhraṃ dabhnoteḥ*', says Yāska (Ni. 3-20). She makes clear the not-smallness: I, Romaśā, am with abundant hair; therefore I am *sarvā* — complete in all limbs. As an example for the hairiness: *gandhārīṇām avikā iva* — as the ewes of Gandhāra, of that country, are woolly, so am I; the country [is to be thought of]. Or else: like the womb of pregnant women, which, since it is forbidden by the śāstra to cut the hair [of that part] until delivery, is hairy — hence this comparison. Since this is so, therefore come to me; do not think of me [as immature]: that is the sense."

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *(Bho pate)* — O husband; *me* — me; *upa upa* — [come] near well; *parā mṛśa* — touch well; *me* — my (limbs); *dabhrāṇi* — small (few) things; *mā manyathāḥ* — do not think; *aham* — I; *gandhārīṇām avikā iva* — like a ewe of the Gandhāra country (or like the womb of the pregnant woman); *romaśā* — hairy; (*ataḥ* — therefore); *sarvā* — with developed limbs; *asmi* — I am.

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** O husband, come to me and touch (my limbs); I am hairy like the ewe of the Gandhāra country (or like the wombs of pregnant women); therefore I am of mature limbs; so do not think me immature.

### Printed p. 247  (PDF 268)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 11.)*

**Printed English (as printed):** *Approach me, (husband); deem me not immature: I am covered with down like a ewe of the Gandharins.* *(sic: "Gandharins")*

**Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 7.**

***dabhrāṇi*** — the word *dabhra* is recorded among the names of "small" (Ni. 3-13 [?]; as printed "೩-೧೩"). *Dabhram arbhakam ity alpasya | dabhraṃ dabhnoteḥ sudambhaṃ bhavati* (Ni. 3-20): from the root *dambh*, meaning "to destroy", the word *dabhra* gives the meaning "small", "little": that is, "easily destroyed". In the present ṛk Bhāvayavya's wife says that she is not such a tender one, but a grown woman fit for enjoyment. For the explanation of this word the author of the Nirukta has cited this very ṛk (Ni. 3-20).

***gandhārīṇām avikā iva romaśā*** — gives two meanings. First: "a ewe of the Gandhāra country, one with exceedingly abundant hair". Second: "one with hair like the womb of a pregnant woman".

Since the main idea of this ṛk and the particulars connected with it have been included in the special topics of the preceding ṛk and translated there, I give here only the commentary of Durgācārya, the commentator on the Nirukta:

> उपोप मे परामृश .... । भावयव्यस्येयमार्षम् । अनुष्टुप् । भावयव्यमेव सा भर्तारं तेनानुपेयमाना ब्रवीति । हे राजन् उपगम्य उपस्पृश्य च मे मम परामृश यः प्रदेशः पुरुषेण प्रियया परामृष्टव्यः । किंच मा मे दभ्राणि मन्यथाः अल्पकानि लोमानि मा मन्यथाः । जानेऽहमेतत् । यथा अलोमिकाया उपगमः प्रतिषिद्धः स्मृतौ — "नाजातलोम्नीमुपहासमिच्छेत्" इति । यते वेदयामि सर्वाहमस्मि रोमशा सर्वेष्वङ्गेषु मदीयान्युत्पन्नानि रोमाणि येषु कामो [?] मुत्सृजन्ते [?] । कथं च पुनरहमस्मि रोमशा ? गन्धारीणामिवाविका गन्धारदेशजातानामविकानां मध्ये या सुष्ठु रोमशा भवेत् तथाहमस्मि रोमशा, निःशङ्को मामुपगच्छेत्यभिप्रायः ॥

> *upopa me parāmṛśa .... | bhāvayavyasyeyamārṣam | anuṣṭup | bhāvayavyameva sā bhartāraṃ tenānupeyamānā bravīti | he rājan upagamya upaspṛśya ca me mama parāmṛśa yaḥ pradeśaḥ puruṣeṇa priyayā parāmṛṣṭavyaḥ | kiṃca mā me dabhrāṇi manyathāḥ alpakāni lomāni mā manyathāḥ | jāne 'hametat | yathā alomikāyā upagamaḥ pratiṣiddhaḥ smṛtau — "nājātalomnīmupahāsamicchet" iti | yate vedayāmi sarvāhamasmi romaśā sarveṣvaṅgeṣu madīyānyutpannāni romāṇi yeṣu kāmo [?] mutsṛjante [?] | kathaṃ ca punarahamasmi romaśā ? gandhārīṇāmivāvikā gandhāradeśajātānāmavikānāṃ madhye yā suṣṭhu romaśā bhavet tathāhamasmi romaśā, niḥśaṅko māmupagacchetyabhiprāyaḥ ‖*

*(Read from the image; the Nirukta commentary is in small type, the words marked [?] are doubtful, and the quotation from the Smṛti "nājātalomnīm upahāsam iccheta" is as printed — I do not complete the Smṛti words.)* "'*Upopa me parāmṛśa*': this is Bhāvayavya's [verse]; Anuṣṭubh. She, the wife, urged by her husband Bhāvayavya … says: 'O king, coming near and touching me, *parāmṛśa* — the region which a man should touch with the beloved … And do not think *dabhrāṇi* — small hairs; I know this: just as in the Smṛti the approach to a woman without hair is forbidden, "one should not seek sport with her whose hair has not grown"; therefore I tell you: *sarvāham asmi romaśā* — I am hairy in all limbs, my hairs have grown in those [places] … And how am I hairy? *Gandhārīṇām ivāvikā* — as, among the ewes born in the Gandhāra country, the one that is well covered with wool, so I am hairy; come to me without fear': this is the intention."

The subject of this ṛk has been introduced in the explanation of the preceding ṛk: in order to establish that she is not a girl but a young woman fit for union, Romaśā says that the hair that indicates youth has grown on her limbs, and gives the example of the ewe of Gandhāra.

…To make this firm the commentator has cited the Smṛti sentence *nājātalomopahāsam iccheta* — that a maiden whose hair has not yet grown on the womb and the other parts is not fit for union.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 7; noted briefly, numbers as read by the OCR).** *me* — by the statement "*vivakṣataḥ kārakāṇi bhavanti*" the dative is used in the sense of the accusative. *mṛśa* — root *mṛśa āmarśane*; Tudādi (*āmarśana* = touching); loṭ second person singular; *tiṅ-nighāta* after a non-verb word. *dabhrāṇi* — root *dambhu dambhane*; *sthāyitañcivañci…* [print: "ಸ್ಥಾಯಿತಂಚಿವಂಚಿ", Uṇ. 2-?] gives *rak*; since *kit*, *anidito hala upadhāyāḥ kṅiti* elides the nasal of the penultimate; final-acute by the suffix; accusative plural. *manyathāḥ* — root *manu avabodhane*; Divādi; laṅ second person singular; since *mā* is connected, *na māṅyoge* (Pā. 6-4-74) gives no augment *aṭ*; *tiṅ-nighāta*. *asmi* — root *as bhuvi*; laṭ first person singular; *tiṅ-nighāta*. *romaśā* — *romāṇi asyāḥ santi iti romaśā*; because it belongs to the *lomādi* group, *lomādipāmādipicchādibhyaḥ śanelacaḥ* (Pā. 5-2-100) gives the suffix *śa*; final-acute by the suffix accent; in the feminine *ṭāp*. *avikā* — *avir eva avikā*; suffix *ka* in the sense of itself; final-acute by the suffix accent. ‖ 7 ‖

## Sūkta 127 — *agniṃ hotāram* (begins at the head of printed p. 249; the Anuvāka 19 opens here)

### Printed p. 249  (PDF 270)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 12 [as read].)*

**ನೂರ ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತೇಳನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು — Nūra ippattēḷaneya sūktavu** (the one hundred and twenty-seventh Sūkta).

*(This Sūkta opens with a long Kannada introduction on the ṛṣi Paruccheṣa, on the style of his ṛks and on their use in the śastra; the Sanskrit introduction (*bhūmikā*) of Sāyaṇa and the table follow later. I give the Kannada in translation.)*

With this Sūkta the nineteenth Anuvāka of the first Maṇḍala begins. In this Anuvāka there are 7 Sūktas, 127 to 133. In the next Anuvāka, the twentieth, there are 6 Sūktas, 134 to 139. The ṛṣi of all the 13 Sūktas of these two Anuvākas is Paruccheṣa Daivodāsi, that is, the son of Divodāsa, named Paruccheṣa. We have already explained about Divodāsa: Divodāsa or Divodāsa Atithigva is a king of very ancient times (the Vedic age). He was the son of Vadhryaśva and the father of Sudās [as read: "ವದ್ಧ್ರ್ಯಶ್ವ … ಸುವಾಸ" — the names are small and I give them as I read]. His name occurs in many places in the Ṛgveda. The chief enemy of this Divodāsa was Śambara, or Dāsa, the leader of the forest people who lived in hills and mountains; this is said there. The sūktas seen by Divodāsa himself are not found anywhere in the Ṛgveda. Therefore modern scholars differ in opinion whether his son, the ṛṣi Paruccheṣa, is the seer of these sūktas. Be that as it may, according to the Anukramaṇī — *agnimīḷādaśa paruccheṣo daivodāsirāgneyaṃ tu pārucchepaṃ sarvam atyaṣṭaṃ tatrādyātiśakvarī …* [as read; the last word, "ṣaṣṭhīti", is doubtful] — it is established that the ṛṣi of all 13 Sūktas (127–139) is Paruccheṣa. Yāska says in his Nirukta —

> परुच्छेप ऋषिः । पर्ववच्छेपः परुषिपरुषि शेपोऽस्येति वा ।

> *parucchepa ṛṣiḥ | parvavacchepaḥ paruṣiparuṣi śepo 'syeti vā |*

(Ni. 10-42, as printed "೧೦-೪೨"; the OCR reads "१०-४३".) That is, because he grew up in great comfort, [he had] a *śepa* in every joint, i.e., one endowed with good development in all the limbs and joints: such is the main idea. The literal sense of the word *paruccheṣa* here is not so important. The story of this ṛṣi is told in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa (Adhyāya 22, Khaṇḍa 5–6) and in the Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa (13-4-5). In these 13 Sūktas seen by Paruccheṣa there are in all 100 ṛks. [A statement about the son of Paruccheṣa, Ānānata Pāruccheṣi, follows:] Ānānataḥ Pāruccheṣi is the seer of the ṛks 1–[?] of the 1[?]th Sūkta of the ninth maṇḍala [as printed; numerals small]. All these ṛks have a special feature of their own. They are in the metres Atyaṣṭi, Atiśakvarī and Atidhṛti, the plural count of which is… The 127th sūkta is of the metre Atiśakvarī; the rest of the sūktas (except some ṛks) are composed in Atyaṣṭi. Such metres have 8 *pādas* and in all 6[?]… syllables, with an addition or deficiency of one or two syllables in some contexts. We have described the characteristics of these metres with examples in Ṛk Saṃhitā, part 1, pp. 221–231. Another peculiarity of the ṛks seen by Paruccheṣa — Yāska says —
